en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Songyuan:
It is a time-honored custom of the monastic community that the patriarchal masters who proclaim the Dharma each have their own recorded sayings. Some may ask: "Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha;
Vimalakīrti remained silent in Vaiśālī; and when the Patriarch came from the West, he transmitted the direct pointing alone. What, then, is there to be taken [from these records]?"
Within the realm of speech and written characters, there may appear differences; yet the Way is but one. Whether speaking or remaining silent, what distinction can there be?
Among the great elders of the Zen school, their preaching was like clouds and rain. Among later students, there have been many who attained realization by means of their words.
To take a recent example: Duofu’s [Wang] realization regarding a single grove of bamboo was his awakening to the Precious Enlightenment (Baobao).
This is the gateway. "The mountain flows upon the water" is the gateway to enlightenment for Miaoxi. Xuansha’s words were realized through awakening by Old Man Linyuan;
Fenyang’s words were realized through awakening by Ganlumei. It is the triggering of karmic conditions that brings about such inspiration.

When arrowpoints meet directly, how can there be any distinction between speech and silence? Master Songyuan possessed a solitary and lofty Dharma-eye and was endowed with correct knowledge and vision;
for thirty years, his every movement regarding the almsbowl served as a standard for the weight of affairs across all quarters.
After the Master passed away, his successor Huizú compiled his lifetime teachings. Furthermore, Master Huanglong Yiweng...
I have compiled their profound essentials into a single volume. Having carefully examined it from beginning to end, I find that every part upholds the supreme pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs;
its guidance for people is most profound and earnest. I have long associated with this Master, whose character is naturally sincere and steadfast, and whose realization is upright and substantial.
In guiding his junior disciples, he relies solely on the realization of one's own original nature.
I have observed that he never once used words or facial expressions to show favoritism toward monastics; rather, he dedicated himself solely to upholding the Dharma. Alas!
As the Buddha-way declined, who other than this Master could have grasped the essence of Miman and thereby sustained the true lineage of Yangqi?
Someone asked: "Of the Chan Master’s thousands of words and myriad phrases, do they not all simply serve to reveal the broken sand-pot?"
Sima. Tut! An unperforated iron hammer.
Written in the tenth month of the third year of the Jiatai era (1203 CE). Humble preface by Qiao Lingxian of Huai’an.
Master Songyuan addressed his disciples, saying: "I have told you clearly: when the mouth opens, it is not upon the tongue. Thief.

The corruption had already been exposed, yet the students did not understand; they cut short the very life-essence of the teaching and instead recorded its superfluous remnants until they had formed a massive volume.
I took it into Longfeng and requested that he compile and arrange it. I observed it closely and saw how the "broken sand-basin" was being treated with such contempt and disdain.
Seeing the core of the matter so clearly, I could not bear it. Although I wished to conceal this family disgrace, it was impossible to do so. However, it is a family shame...
"Thirty years from now, there will surely be one who vindicates this injustice.
Written respectfully on the Double Ninth day of the third year of Jiatai (the year of Guihai), by the bhikṣu Qingru, a dharma younger brother residing at Huanglong Mountain.
When the World-Honored One held up a flower, Kāśyapa smiled. Examining this closely, it is evident that there was already no small amount of leakage.
Therefore, Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout were intended to utterly destroy one's own spirit; how could they allow for any deliberation or even a hair’s breadth of separation between them?
In recent times, the masters of our school have abandoned both intellectual understanding and emotional attachment, and the path of words has been cut off.
To carry the burden of the Buddha-dharma and be able to awaken those who come after—how rare!
As for the Elder Songyuan, whom could one turn to for refuge? Songyuan and I shared a long-standing friendship;
he himself said that before leaving home and receiving full ordination, he attained a profound realization under Master Ying’an Hua, and later followed Master Muguan Yong.
Master Gong and Master Miaoyan Jie, as well as various spiritual teachers he visited, had repeatedly brought about insights and awakenings in him;

yet, he still harbored doubts because he felt he had not yet attained a state of total liberation. This continued for many years, during which he exerted himself with such rigorous self-discipline that he forgot both cold and heat.
One day, while staying under the guidance of Master Quan at Daochang Monastery, he suddenly attained realization, and the web of his doubts was completely cleared away.

At that time, Master Quan had gone abroad on a fundraising journey; several days later, he returned. [Changqing] urgently sought confirmation of his realization and entered the room ahead of the assembly.
However, Master Quan’s spiritual pivot did not align with his, so Songyuan scolded him and sent him out. He immediately packed his bags and traveled to Fengkou to visit Mian.
Before he had time to speak, Miman said, "I am glad that the Great Matter has been clarified; once it is voiced, it becomes unfitting.
Thereupon, Songyuan returned to the hall to rest. As he departed from the meditation hall, he spoke this verse: "The first move at the head is without any ambiguity."
Coming and going are like waves upon the water; when there is spirit, let it be augmented by further spirit. Let them teach that one may raise weapons even on level ground.
From Chêng-chao to Hsien-ch'in and Pao-ts'i, there were eight who occupied the monasteries.

When I saw Sōng-yüan while he was still in good health, he joyfully referred to himself as a disciple in training (*śaikṣa*) alongside Kuan-mu, Ta-ch'ün, and Hui-tsu. Now, regarding Hui-tsu, because of him—
The Master’s discourse records have been brought to me for a preface. Consequently, I shall record the origins and development of his teacher’s attainment of the Way.
I alone find it strange that Huanglong Ruqing, having clearly understood the message that Songyuan had conveyed—that "opening one's mouth is not upon the tongue"—[yet still fell into error].

These remaining words ought to have been cast aside and extinguished like shadows, their traces utterly severed. Yet now they have been compiled and arranged, broadcasting the family’s disgrace to the outside world.
I fear that in days to come, those who treat Songyuan with neglect will find that Huanglong cannot escape his responsibility.
Postscript by Meng You of Ji Jun on the eighth day of the twelfth month in the Guihai year of the Jiatai era.
The table of contents follows in three sections.
Volume One:
Record of Sayings from Chengzhao Chan Monastery at Yangshan, Pingjiang Prefecture;
Record of Sayings from Ba’en Guangxiao Chan Temple on Mount Jun, Jiangyin Commandery.
Recorded Sayings of the Wujun Yezhufu Shan Jishi Chan Monastery;
Recorded Sayings of the Jianfu Chan Monastery in Raoyou;
Recorded Sayings of the Zhidu Chan Monastery at Xiangshan in Mingzhou.
Recorded Sayings of Yunyan Chan Monastery on Mount Huqiu in Pingjiang Prefecture,
Volume Lower;
Recorded Sayings of Jingde Lingyin Chan Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture.
Recorded Sayings of the Founder of Xianqin Baoci Chan Temple;
Sermons on Holding the Whisk; Universal Dharma Discourses; Verses on Ancient Cases; Eulogies for Buddhas and Patriarchs;
Gāthās; Epitaphs and Postscripts.
The Recorded Sayings of Master Songyuan, Volume One:
The Record of the Chan Monastery Chengzhao at Yangshan in Pingjiang Prefecture,
compiled by the students of the Way, Shanka, Guangmu, and others.

While serving as the Head Seat at Lingyin Monastery, the Master accepted an invitation. Holding up the formal letter, he said: "The sword that kills, the blade that gives life—the Patriarchal Command is being put into action;
let this serve as the proof."
Holding up the Dharma robe, he said: "At midnight at Huangmei, atop Dayu Ridge, clenching his teeth and grinding his jaw, pulling the plow and tugging the handle—why was it thus?
Calamity does not enter the door of the prudent."
Pointing to the Dharma-seat, he said: "The emptiness of all dharmas is the seat. When walking, one walks together with all people;
when sitting, one sits together with all people. Do you, all of you, see the Tathāgata Sumerudīparāja? Behold, I shall now set forth the model and delineate the likeness."
The Master ascends the seat. A monk asks: "I do not ask about the midnight at Huangmei; what of the matter of pulling the plow? The Master replies:

"Even the Buddha’s hand cannot block it. The monk presses further: "If that is so, then the bright sun is already in the sky. The Master replies: "Squeezing one's eyes until flowers appear before them.
The monk presses further: "Buddha to Buddha, hand to hand; Patriarch to Patriarch, transmission to transmission. I wonder, what exactly is being transmitted? The Master raises [his staff].
[The Master] raises his whisk. [The Guest] advances and says, "If that is so, what of the Seven Patriarchs of India and the Two or Three Patriarchs of the Tang land?

[The Master] replies, "A point may reach, but it does not arrive. [The Guest] advances and says, "If it is not the true offspring of the blind donkey, how can one succeed to this school's tradition? [The Master] replies, "..."
Upon arriving, he did not light the lamp. A monk asked, "When Baoshou opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk, and Baoshou immediately struck him.

What was the meaning of this? He replied, "Biting down on his teeth. The monk pressed further, "Sansheng said, 'If you act as a teacher in this way, you will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou.
What about that? He replied, "Opening his mouth reveals his gallbladder. The monk pressed further, "The Dragon..."

The sleeves are swept aside and the whole body is revealed; where the Elephant King walks, the tracks of the foxes vanish. He replied, "One must strictly avoid following the heterodox or pursuing the evil.
He pressed further, "I do not yet understand: how about Xin Chengzhao? He replied, "Iron banners and iron drums. He pressed further.
He opens wide the paths of the Three Essentials and Three Mysteries; who else can hold fast the heavens and earth? The Master said, "Wrong. The monk bowed.
The Master then said, "In the kingdom of Magadha, we have already exhausted flowery words; before the peak of Shaoshi, we have merely passed each other by in dullness.
Thus, one receives echoes in the void and brandishes staffs and shouts. Revealing great potential and clarifying great function, he points directly face-to-face—vivid and agile."
*Fak*. Gain and loss are both lost; right and wrong have utterly vanished. Used upside down or grasped crosswise, there is a standard for the immediate occasion.
Each and every thing flows forth from within one's own breast, covering heaven and earth. Thus, when a single speck of dust arises, the entire great earth is fully contained.
A single phrase is without self-interest; it fully manifests the Precious Seal. Although this is so, it is still but a partial presentation.
But tell me, what is the occasion of the full presentation? [He plants his staff. "The green mountains do not lock their soaring momentum; the vast ocean surely knows its source is high."
Again, he raised the matter of the Three Holy Paths. Xuedou said, "Whenever I meet someone, I come out; when I come out, I do not act for others.
Xinghua also said, "Whenever I meet someone, I do not come out; when I come out, I immediately act for others.

The Master said, "Those who tread upon this single path will know that these two old fellows both wish to hold hands and walk together, yet they cannot avoid each setting off toward their own destination."—Xin Chengzhao.
As soon as he encounters someone, he comes forth; having come forth, he immediately acts for the sake of others. He does not treat the Buddha-dharma as a mere social favor.
Just look at what kind of time it is now! With a shout, he descended from his seat.
Entering the Gate. Pointing to the three gates, he said: "To see once is to see forever; to attain once is to attain eternally.
The eighty-four thousand Dharma-gates all enter through this very gate. He let out a shout.
Entering the Buddha Hall, he burned incense and said: "Mañjuśrī rides a lion; Samantabhadra rides an elephant; Kāśyapa raises his fists; Ānanda joins his palms.
But tell me, how thick is the skin on the face of this old man of yellow hue? Heh! Thereupon, he prostrated himself.
The Great Minister, the Provincial Governor, presented a memorial. The Master rose and showed it to the assembly, saying:
"The treasury of the great liberation and the samādhi-gate of inexhaustibility—the pure entrustment of Vulture Peak—is all contained herein. Do you see it?"
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time occupy this seat to fully uphold the Seal of Orthodoxy;
the patriarchal masters of successive generations occupy this seat to preach the 'Great Empty Talk. Now tell me, how should one act today? Much emptiness is not as good as little reality.
He then ascended the seat and, holding up the incense, said: "This single offering of incense, I respectfully offer for..."
For the two Palaces and the Emperor, I pray for the prolongation of their sagely years. I reverently wish that the wind of Yao may spread forever and the sun of Shun may shine eternally.

Again, holding up the incense, he said: "This single offering of incense is respectfully offered for the Chancellor, the Palace Aide, the Right Minister, the Palace Commissioner, the Chief Minister, and all the noble officials, to exalt their venerable years."

Again, he held up the incense and said: "This single offering of incense is no longer to be hidden away; I offer it directly for the Great Abbot Miaokuan, who formerly resided at Mount Jing and later resided at Lingyin.
I burn it within this furnace, leaving it entirely to the monks of the world to strike bricks and beat tiles.
He then took his seat. After the mallet was struck to signal the beginning of the assembly, he said: "The primary truth has been shattered by a single blow of the mallet."

Is there anyone who would not find this agreeable? A monk asked: "As soon as one arrives at Mount Yang, the grasses and trees are in spring; amidst the shadows of the myriad phenomena, not a speck of dust remains.
With doors and windows wide open, sitting facing the hall, the long days are vast and silent—congratulations on this Great Peace!

[This was] a prayer for the Emperor upon opening the hall. "I wish to hear the essential Dharma. He replied: "Heaven is eternal and earth is enduring. The monk pressed further: "Furthermore, take up the unperforated flute of Shaolin..."
"Meeting the wind, it stirs ten-thousand-year joy. [The Master] replied, "Xu You did not wash his ears.
[The Monk] asked, "What is the realm of Yangshan? [The Master] replied, "Those with eyes see it. [The Monk] asked, "Tall pines and bamboos, thin mists gather;
layered peaks and ridges, the moon rises late. [The Master] replied, "You cannot lead me away. [The Monk] asked, "Who is the person within the realm? [The Master] replied, "You."
"Where have you come from? The monk gave a shout. The Master said, "Zha. The monk bowed. The Master then said: "The root of transformation and nourishment:
things and self share the same path. The source of the patriarchs and Buddhas: unchanged through antiquity and today. It is spiritual and uniquely revealed, penetrating form and penetrating sound.
It cuts off all diversities; solitary and precarious, it stands nowhere. Like the sky that covers all, like the earth that supports all. If..."
Whether noble or ordinary, all receive the power of this grace. Therefore, for the sake of benefiting the world, I have proclaimed this Seal of the Dharma in whatever direction it may reach;
do not propagate it recklessly. Today, gods and humans are gathered here in great numbers. Before this assembly, I have clearly and openly revealed it.
Then, raising his whisk, he said: "Do you see? The assembly on Vulture Peak remains as if it had never dispersed. In India and here..."
The transmission of the Dharma is direct and continuous, establishing no rungs on a ladder; it stands alone, pointing beyond the realm of forms. At such a time as this, how is it?
The momentum of a thousand peaks ceases at the foot of the mountain; the sound of ten thousand streams vanishes upon reaching the sea.

To cite another instance: Formerly, when Song Linggong, the Grand Governor of Hongzhou, once requested the monk of Daling Temple to invite the Second Seat to ascend the hall for a formal sermon, the Governor said, "Why do you not invite the First Seat? The assembly of monks was speechless.
Later, Master Baoning Yong remarked, "If I had been there when the Governor asked that question, I would have simply replied to him: 'How would we dare?'"
"Forgive me, Lord Commissioner. The Master said, "The Lord Commissioner holds high the seal of orthodoxy; Baoning has briefly revealed his style and regulations.

With the true eye clearly penetrating, there is no injury to the blade or the hand; naturally, there is the same wind across a thousand miles. But tell me, how do you express this 'same wind' in a single phrase?
"In a year of plenty, the country elders sing of the abundance; in the great transformation of non-action, the Way is at peace."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "Entering a field of weeds, one does not discriminate; reaching out with the hand, one simply grasps the grass.
The long is the Dharma-body of length; the short is the Dharma-body of shortness. Do you all understand this? (He struck the ground with the staff. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Three people have taken a tortoise for a turtle; though they have mouths, they cannot speak. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, the waves surge;
within the vast ocean, one is scorched by fire. Part! Part! The golden-skinned dhūta has already leaked the secret. He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If you offer the Buddha-dharma as an offering, it will drag all of you into hell faster than an arrow.

If you offer worldly dharmas as an offering, your elders will have their eyebrows and beards fall out. You will sit in one place and walk seven paces; you will be horizontal in three ways and vertical in four;
you will strip away the skull-cap and your eyes will bulge out. Now tell me, are you ordinary people or sages? He raised his staff, struck it once, and shouted.
A shout! I invite the Chief Cook and the Hall Master to ascend the hall. The spring breeze sweeps vast and free; it is the model of the ancient Buddhas. The spring waters flow with a murmur;
look quickly with your eyes! A lantern leaps into a pillar; a Buddha hall strides out through the triple gate, bumping into someone without a face.

"Look at this! It is said that 'a multitude of mouths are difficult to harmonize. One must be able to pivot with subtle mastery according to the occasion. Great assembly, tell me: how does one pivot when the occasion arises?
Suddenly picking up his staff, he said: "Whether it be right or wrong, people do not know; whether it be acting contrary to or in accord with the flow, even Heaven cannot fathom it.
He struck the ground with the staff and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The superior person, upon hearing the Way, practices it with diligence. The man who plays with clods of mud.

The middling person, upon hearing the Way, is as if it exists and yet as if it is lost—a single stroke, two pieces. The inferior person, upon hearing the Way, laughs at it—a colorful, frantic, and muddled household.
Chengzhao makes this announcement: tell me, where does the crux lie? A sharp blade cuts the flesh, yet the wound still heals; but malicious words—"
"The wound remains, and the resentment does not fade.

He ascended the hall and said: "If you can realize it under the first phrase, even Buddhas and Patriarchs will beg for their lives. If you can realize it under the second phrase, the heavenly demons' hearts will shatter.
If you can realize it under the third phrase, you will cast yourself across the jaws of a tiger. He then took up his staff, held it horizontally, and said:
If people proceed in this manner, they cannot avoid binding themselves without ropes. But tell me, where does the point of danger lie?
If one does not sleep on the same bed, how can one know what is pierced within the covers?
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: “As for the Buddha-dharma and the Way of Chan, to cast them all at once into Lake Tai might not seem rash;
yet one day the alms bowl becomes wet twice. Truly, not even a single drop can be dispensed with. Why?
Because a patch-robed monk must first have his own belly full before he can succeed. *Du!* (A shout).”
Ascending the hall on the Emperor’s Birthday: Heaven is infinitely high; in that infinity there is a Honored One. Earth is boundlessly thick; in that boundlessness there is a Sovereign.

Within his breast he harbors the six directions; within his sleeves lie heaven and earth. He manifests a great potential and displays a great function; he practices the teaching of the unspoken and inaugurates the transformation of non-action.
For this reason, the Buddhas appeared in the world and the Patriarchs came from the West—some plucking a flower, some holding up a whisk.
Some face the wall; they do not establish written words, but point directly and transmit alone. This, too, is merely to clarify this very principle of non-action (*wuwei*).

May its blessings flow through the sands of the world, and may its celebration be inherited by one person. Do you understand this thoroughly? Its brilliance matches the North Pole; its span of life equals Mount Nan.
Ascending the hall, he raised [this case]: An ancient worthy said, "If you follow conditions like the wind, flying sand and rolling stones do not deviate from space.
Simply be unimpeded regarding phenomena and there is no phenomenon; seeing forms and hearing sounds, one need not be deaf. Thus did the ancient worthy announce it.
This is truly what is meant by "pressing the ox's head while it eats grass. If you are Chengzhao, who could possibly control you?

When asked about the West, you answer from the East; let people laugh and say I am feigning deafness. White clouds may briefly leave the green peaks, but the bright moon cannot be made to descend from the azure sky.
I request the administrative official to ascend the hall. Blinking one's eyebrows—there is no room for deliberation. To shoulder this burden crosswise, it must be the person themselves;
disregarding peril and ruin, they "pinpoint the one and strike the two," settling matters upon the turning wheel of the pivot without erring by even a hair’s breadth.
Although this is so, it is still but the ordinary tea and rice of the patch-robed monks. But tell me, what is it ultimately like? The Great Garuda spreads its wings.
The wings and canopies cover the ten continents; by the hedge, the swallows and sparrows chirp in vain. Entering the hall, he said:
"Of all the various arrangements one could devise, none are better than the ordinary. It neither startles people, yet it endures for a long time. He gave a shout and said:
"What is there to say about long duration? After a long silence, he struck his knee and said, "Who would have known that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is yet another way of thinking?
He then descended from his seat.
The Record of the Sayings of the Chan Master of Baen Gwanghyo Temple on Geumgang Mountain, Jiangyin Circuit.
Compiled by the students of the Way: Sanae, Gwangmuk, and others.
Pointing to the three gates, he said: "There is a path to Geumgang Mountain, yet those who reach it are rare. Since liberation has no gate, by what means does one enter?"
[He] lets out a shout and says: "One blind man leads a crowd of blind men into the Buddha Hall.
[Then he] burns incense and says: "Deshan demolished the Buddha Hall; Yunmen struck him so that even a dog would eat it—this was not considered excessive.
When Elder Yue arrived, he cut them all off at once; yet, for the time being, he harmonized with the light."
Dust! Let the Yellow-Faced Old Man naturally bow his brow to the ground.
Taking his seat in the abbot’s quarters, he said: "The vast void hangs its sword, fully wielding life and death; like a shooting star or a flash of lightning, mist and clouds part asunder.
Among them all, who is the one who emerges? With a single long cry, heaven and earth are wide open."
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The boundless realms of all lands are seen upon the tip of a single hair; without traversing the journey, one has already arrived home.
What is the phrase for having arrived home? He replied: "The moon is like a drawn bow; little rain, much wind. The monk pressed further:
"If it were not for one with eyes who possesses the Jade Hall, they would not easily reach Mount Junshan. He replied: "I walk amidst the wild weeds; you, moreover..."
He entered a deep village. The monk stepped forward and said, "I thank the Master for his reply.

The Master then gave a shout. The monk bowed. The Master then raised the following case: When Baoshou opened the hall for his first sermon, Sansheng pushed forward a monk; Baoshou struck him immediately. Sansheng said:
"To teach people in such a manner is to blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou. Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
The Master said, "In general, to uphold the Dharma-lineage, one must possess the true eye atop the head and the efficacious talisman behind the elbow.
When these two venerable elders casually jostled and pressed one another, they immediately revealed the very marrow of Linji’s mind. Only—
This is because they do not realize that life and nature are entirely in the hands of this monk. Is there anyone who can examine this and discern it?
In years past, seeking fire, he obtained it along with the smoke; today, carrying water from the spring, he returns with the moon.
Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally across his chest and said: "Maitreya, the true Maitreya, manifests a thousand billion emanations.

From time to time he reveals himself to those of this age, yet people of this age all fail to recognize him. Have you all recognized him yet? To see him and not take [the opportunity]—this is a great pity."
A thousand years hence, this will not be forgotten. He then cast down his staff, descended from the seat, and ascended the hall.
"When a person of heterodoxy speaks the True Dharma, the True Dharma is entirely heterodox; when a person of orthodoxy speaks heterodox dharma, the heterodox dharma is entirely true.
Suddenly grasping his staff, he struck it once and said: "What place is this? To speak of heterodoxy or..."
"True. Nevertheless, those who laugh at me are many; those who smile at me are few. Thereupon, he leaned on his staff and descended from the seat. Ascending the hall, [the Master said:
"The sword that kills and the sword that gives life—this was the standard of antiquity and the essential pivot of the present age.
When the ancients spoke thus, they were far too timid. This mountain monk is a hundred ugly and a thousand clumsy; stumbling and dragging along, there is no killing here either."
"The human blade, the living sword—this was simply because at that time I lacked the skillful means while traveling on pilgrimage.
I kicked over a single broken sand-pot, and even until now it cannot be picked up. Is there anyone among you who can pick it up? He gave a shout.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Whether there is profit or loss, one does not leave the marketplace. When Mr. Zhang drinks the wine, Mr. Li gets drunk; there is a reason for stretching out one's legs to sleep.
As soon as one tries to be wide awake, it becomes a taboo. It is not non-being, yet it is not being; it is not right, yet it is not wrong.

When encountering the noble, one acts humble; when encountering the humble, one acts noble. The tabby cat and the white ox recite the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*. The Patriarch did not understand the meaning of the West."
On the eighth day of the fourth month, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "The Yellow-Faced Old Man has descended to birth;
he is right now at the tip of this staff. Pointing one finger toward heaven and one finger toward earth, he said: "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored. Do you all see him?
If you say you see him, you have been thoroughly deceived by this staff. If you say you do not see him, [you are likewise deceived].
People deceive themselves. Relying on the staff, he descends from his seat.
Entering the hall, he says: "The first day of the month is called the New Moon; the full moon is called the Full Moon. With the eight characters wide open, there is both gathering in and letting go.
Two thousand years ago, Śākyamuni’s true eye at the crown of Maheśvara’s head was held up face-to-face—raw iron.
The threshold. A man of brilliance would lift his robe and pass straight through; as for the lacquered bucket, let it carry its wooden board as it pleases.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and leaned it across his chest, saying: "One is not it; two is not it either. The eyes protrude, yet the nose is lost.
At Shaolin, they stubbornly sought to settle the mind; the blind donkey did not receive the prediction of Vulture Peak."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example, saying: "Master Nanquan said, 'Since I was young, I have raised a water buffalo.
If I intend to let it loose on the east side of the stream, it will inevitably eat the king’s grass and drink the king’s water.

If I intend to let it loose on the west side of the stream, it will inevitably eat the king’s grass and drink the king’s water. It is better to accept things as they are; yet even this cannot be seen. The Master then said, "Wang..."
The Master has indeed emptied his heart and poured out his guts, yet he has not yet seen a transformation of customs or a change of habits. This mountain monk has raised but a single donkey;
it has always been toppling to the east and staggering to the west. When moving with the times, in a single day it covers no less than a thousand or ten thousand li.
At that moment, he simply took one step and refused to move further. Tell me, how far apart was this from Master Wáng’s water buffalo?
After a long silence, he said: "The fisherman dances with his oars; the rustic old man sings his song."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example. Xuedou’s verse for Dao Risen said: "Three parts of the light have already passed; The single point of the numinous platform remains unpolished.
In pursuit of life, one rushes about in vain day after day; If one does not turn back when called, what can be done?
He turns the celestial wheel, shifts the terrestrial axis, takes south as north, and cuts through iron and hews down nails. This belongs to that old fellow Xuedou alone. Only—
"It is not fitting to sit here. (He gives a shout. He ascends the hall:
"A field of a thousand years has eight hundred owners; the dilapidated house has no one to repair it. Even where there is no elegance, there is elegance.
If you go on like this, the entire school of Bodhidharma will be swept away to nothingness."

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "A thousand explanations and ten thousand expositions are not equal to seeing for oneself. Break open the lacquer bucket! What is it that comes from the Hu and manifests as a Han?
There are a certain kind of people who understand it in just this way; they hold fast to their view to the end and refuse to let go.

This is truly what is meant by 'the numinous tortoise bearing the map' or 'the phoenix entangled in a golden net. As soon as they are pressed by others, they cannot distinguish black from white; muddled and confused, they instead claim to 'force the good to submit.'"
Wretched! To have let this one life pass in vain—tell me, how can such a person be saved? Striking his knees with both hands, he said:
"When the dragon gains the water, its spirit increases; when the tiger encounters the mountain scenery, its fierce majesty grows."
Ascending the hall upon leaving the hospital: A lifetime’s livelihood rests on a single thread; Singing to the moon and welcoming the wind, one attains freedom.
Who cares for the clear river rising against the tide? With ease, one strides across the vast blue sea.
Record of the Sayings of Wujun Yefu Shan Jishi Chan Monastery;
compiled by the students of the Way, Puyan, et al. Entering the Monastery:
Pointing to the Main Gate, he said: "The wondrous function extends horizontally and vertically, cutting off the ten directions. Those who have not yet mastered this pulse, when they take a step..."
Still difficult. Behold this new elder acting foolishly here! [He] lets out a shout and enters the abbot’s quarters.
Taking his seat, he says: "The abbot's quarters of Yefu are entirely without obstruction; fist and kick correspond, and one does not yield to another.
Wondrously turning, a continuous single pulse flows through—who would have known that the Linji lineage has been extinguished?"

He ascended the seat. Having offered incense and made his vow for the Emperor (the questions and answers are not recorded), he then said: "The mind-seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox; when it departs, it is immediately sealed."
To abide is to break the seal. This is why Bodhidharma did not come to the Eastern Land and the Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven.
Among the seven hundred eminent monks of Huangmei, the robe and bowl were entrusted to Layman Lu. Lamp after lamp continued the succession; subject and object were both forgotten.
Pointing directly and transmitted alone—how truly sublime is this style! Do you understand thoroughly? Having traveled the south of the Yangtze and everywhere north of it, he has caught the wind.

[The Master] continued with a verse: "In the place of flowing, let there be elegance" (having finished his expressions of thanks). He then raised another case. A monk asked Baizhang, "What is the extraordinary matter?
Baizhang said, "Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. The monk bowed, and Baizhang struck him. The Master said, "Mounting the tiger’s head, he gathers up the tiger’s tail."
I return this to Old Man Baizhang. If we discuss extraordinary matters, there will inevitably be some points of confusion.
Can you all discern them? When winter is not yet cold, look after the twelfth lunar month.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Do not seek it in the Buddha; do not seek it in the Dharma; do not seek it in the Sangha. This is still merely holding the mooring line while letting the boat drift.

It scatters white clouds and pierces the azure void; its rushing current surpasses the blade, and its swift flame exceeds the wind. Yet this does not yet suffice under the gate of the patch-robed monk.
But tell me, how is it ultimately? Let the vast ocean change as it may, I shall never speak for you."
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Yangqi said, "Yangqi has newly settled; the walls of the house are thin and sparse. The entire hall is covered with snow and true pearls.
Shrink your necks and sigh in secret. I recall the ancients dwelling beneath the trees. Master Yangqi only knew how to gather them in.
Not liberated. When Yezhu first took up residence, who was distant and who was intimate? Taking the non-existent as existent, he was fully host and fully guest.
He harmonized with the light and shared in the dust. Who says that the golden needle is not given to others? (He lets out a shout.)
Ascending the hall, he said: "The teaching style of Yaofu has no special principles. It is simply rice from one's own fields, sleeping early and rising late;
washing the face and touching the nose, sipping tea and moistening the mouth. If someone were suddenly to come forward and say, 'Lower your voice!
Lower your voice! The walls have ears!'—one cannot even blame them. Why? Because the Buddha of Dongshan has no light; this is the same as Han Xin appearing at court."
[The Master] gave a shout.
He ascended the hall and said: "I cite: Fenyang addressed the assembly, saying, 'If you recognize this staff, the business of traveling on pilgrimage is finished. The Master said:
Although Fenyang’s opening of his mouth reveals his very heart, he cannot avoid falling into the second place. Suddenly, he picked up the staff and said: "This..."
This cannot be called a staff; it is a lacquered bucket. [End of] inquiry. Entering the hall for the discourse:
"That the Buddhas of the three periods do not know its existence is not beyond what is natural; that the house cat and the white ox, however, do know its existence—[this is extraordinary]."
Adding frost to snow. Three consecutive *qian* hexagrams; six segments of *kun*. Penetrating past and present, there is no obstruction. It is difficult to find a path before the sound [of the shout].
Like a ball rolling on a plate, and a pearl rolling on a plate. *Hè!* (A shout).

Ascending the hall, he raised an example, saying: "The Third Patriarch said: 'If the eyes do not sleep, all dreams vanish of themselves; if the mind does not differ, the myriad dharmas are one suchness.
But what is this 'one suchness'? It is not the hand that shoots down the eagle; it is merely the talk of General Li."
On the twelfth day of the sixth month, the memorial vegetarian feast for the two masters Ying’an and Mian was held. Holding up the incense, he said:
"These two old, frozen sores gnash their teeth and grind their jaws, scattering dust and tossing up soil; they have offenses as vast as the heavens.
For forty years I have wandered through the rivers and lakes, yet I have been too ashamed to enter this protective community. Since I do not enter their protective community, why today..."
With this offering, he then shook his hand and said, "O-yi! O-yi! To whom was this meaning clearly directed?
He ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said: "When the string is moved, the melody is known; when the leaves fall, autumn is known. By citing one, the three are clarified;
the eyes discern the subtlest weights. If you go on like this, Yezhu has not yet let you go. Why? Because the immortal cassia tree in the moon remains with its roots intact.
He pulls it out. He drags the horns from the black dragon at the bottom of the sea.
Entering the hall, he holds up his staff and says: "A thousand explanations and ten thousand expositions are not as good as one decisive resolution. But tell me, what is it that you resolve?"
If you see it directly right now, ninety days of practice will have been spent without waste. If it is not so, then where else can you settle yourself and establish your life?
(He plants his staff firmly. Furthermore, what place could one find lacking in elegance?

Ascending the hall, he said: "To enter directly with a single blade, one is still separated by heavy barriers. To hit the mark a hundred times out of a hundred is merely to crash through walls and strike against battlements.

Even if you were to face south and look at the Big Dipper, and even if those who claim to know it were all overturned—burning incense in the Buddha Hall and joining palms at the main gate, these too fall into the trap of the patch-robed monk. After all, what is it? Touzi then descended from his meditation seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient case: A monk asked Tong’an, “What is the person who has gone forth? An said, “A cold cicada clings to a withered tree;
its weeping is exhausted, yet it does not turn its head. Again he asked, “What is the person who returns?
An said, “Reed flowers bloom amidst the fire; meeting spring, they are just like autumn. Again he asked, “What is the person who neither comes nor goes? An said:
The Stone Ram meets the Stone Tiger; when they encounter one another, how can they ever rest? The Master said:

"To speak deeply of principle and respond to things according to their conditions—this belongs to the old man Tong'an. However, from the standpoint of the Zen monk's school, he cannot avoid falling into a trap.
Why? Because he only knows how to set sail with the wind, but cannot steer against it. Suppose someone were to ask Yefu: "What is 'facing'?"
Regarding the person who has departed, he replied: "The eyes protrude. Regarding the person who returns, he replied: "The heavens are vast and the earth is wide.
Regarding the person who neither departs nor returns, he replied: "The bright moon illuminates the deep valley;
the cold waves echo with the sound of the night mortar. These words leave you nothing to chew upon; you must truly awaken to them before you can understand.
Ascending the hall to open the furnace: A cold moon and frosty sky; the Way is solitary. A community of Chan practitioners tends the cold hearth.
Where the patched robe is torn, ice penetrates the bones. The night is still and deep, and even the charcoal is gone. The ancients were truly far from being considerate of human sentiment.
I, this mountain monk, shall now open up a single thread of the Way. At the monastery gates of Yeyu, the rice and gruel are coarse;
literature and the Buddha-dharma are both absent for a time. In the earthen stove, there is but a little smokeless fire; yet it provides more than enough joy for the practitioners of Zen. (A shout.)
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following case]: Guizong said, "In Guizong, phenomena and principle are cut off; the sun is at its zenith.
Sovereign and free like a lion, it does not rely on external things. The Master said, "Big or small, Guizong’s heels do not touch the ground."

Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: The movement of the sun’s shadow shifts; the sun reaches its longest path to the south. Throughout the four directions and intermediate points, there is celebration and nothing that is not favorable.
But tell me, what is the matter in between? Throwing down his staff, he said: "Just so! Just so!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Snow, snow—clearly and vividly it leaks forth. Withered trees bloom; empty space shatters. The True Person of No Rank is freezing to the bone;
the lanterns and pillars knit their eyebrows together. Suddenly it clears: there is nothing to say. All join in celebration of this auspicious season of abundance."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example: Linji said, "There is one person who remains on the road for kalpas without ever leaving home;

there is another person who leaves home and is no longer on the road. Which of these two deserves the offerings of devas and humans? The Master said, "The eyes look toward the southeast, but the mind is set upon the northwest."
Ascending the hall on the first day of the year: the new beginning of the Primordial Epoch brings all things into manifestation. Sometimes he lets go; sometimes he cuts off.
Without sparing even his two eyebrows, he shifts the sitting platform along with him. Buddhist Dharma and worldly dharma are, in total, a single piece.
Since they are both Buddhist Dharma and worldly dharma, how can they become one? Simply discern the heart of resolve, and you will certainly not be deceived.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: "Liangshan said, 'To those coming from the south, I give thirty blows; to those coming from the north, I give thirty blows.
Although this is so, it does not accord with the essential teaching of our school. Later, Langya said, 'Liangshan possesses a great mass of pure gold.'"
[The Master] was about to sell it as mere scrap iron. Langya, however, was not like this:

he would give thirty blows to those coming from the south and thirty blows to those coming from the north, leaving the monks of the world to criticize him as they pleased. The Master said, "Yezhu was not like this."
"Whether coming from the south or the north, just pass by like this. Suddenly, when the lacquer bucket is broken open, I will give you thirty blows.
He ascended the hall and said: "Clearly you know it is just this; why do you fail to penetrate it? It is simply because of what is beneath your feet."
The red silk thread is unbroken; as soon as one is pressed by others, one cannot turn back.
In a state of resentment and dissatisfaction, there is ultimately a "thing that obstructs the chest," which can neither be pushed forward nor pulled back. How, then, can one break through and escape?
Nanquan’s beheading of the cat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Throughout the thousands and tens of thousands since time immemorial, only one or two have been truly ensnared.
As for the rest, they simply drift along, moving spontaneously; drifting along, moving spontaneously—how could they be fit for debate? Having reported this to you, look now:
are the eyebrows of Yezhu still there? Huṃ! Huṃ!"
Ascending the hall, he raised the verse by Liangshan regarding his whisk, which says: "I have a single whisk, Its true core is made of iron.

It reveals the Way to frighten away mosquitoes and gadflies; Pointing southward, it never yields. It sweeps away the illnesses of Buddhas and Patriarchs, And shatters the lairs of the patch-robed monks.
If one is a person of the highest caliber, One will never call it a mere 'thing'. Deshan remarked, "Liangshan’s verse is fine, but it splits the matter into two parts."
Liangshan said, "That old monk was not careful enough at the time. The Master said, "Those two great elders were truly extraordinary.
To bind what is loose with urgency is easy; to bind what is urgent with looseness is difficult.
Today, Yeyu’s nostrils have fallen into the hands of all of you, so feel free to drag them about however you wish. He let out a shout.

Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: Today we enter the formal retreat. According to the established customs of the monastic community, whether it be a long or short term, one remains as motionless as a pillar and as oblivious as a fool.
Transcending the four propositions and cutting off the hundred negations, everyone gathers together to eat a spoonful of gruel. (He lets out a shout.)
Ascending the hall: This summer, the hall has been cramped; the seats for the superior, middle, and junior monks have pressed against one another.

Suddenly, if a single person were to awaken to the True Source, it would cause everyone to dismantle their homes and scatter their dwellings—save only for the lanterns and the pillars, which would laugh with a "he-he" of cold smiles.
Yet he says, "Such is it. To bring this up in such a way is rare in the world; one must know that there is still one more blow needed behind the head.
[He] ascended the hall and said, citing a case: A monk asked Nan-yuan, "Upon this mass of flesh, ten thousand fathoms stand like a sheer cliff—is this not your own words, Master?
Nan-yuan said, "Yes. The monk overturned the meditation seat. Nan-yuan raised his staff; as the monk hesitated, Nan-yuan struck him and drove him away.
[The monk] stepped forward. The Master said, "This monk is single-mindedly cautious yet dares to let loose his great courage. Old Nanyuan was also a karmic connection for raising a son.

On the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "Today is the Dragon Boat Festival of the fifth month; within the school of the patched-robed monks, there is not a single word to be spoken. A thousand demons..."
A hundred monsters hide their tracks; ten thousand miles of long sky is a single line of iron.
[He] ascends the hall. He cites: A monk asked Yangshan, "Does the Dharma-body know how to preach the Dharma?
Yangshan said, "I cannot preach it. There is one person who can preach it. The monk said, "Where is that person who can preach it? Yangshan pushed him out.
The pillow case. Guishan said, "Jizi is using the business of the sword's edge. The Master said, "Yangshan’s backbone is usually as hard as iron;
yet, being squeezed by this monk two or three times, he immediately fell flat on all fours.
Guishan could not contain his impatience for a moment, and it seems he lost one of his eyes without realizing it. Suddenly, a monk asked Yefu about the Dharma.
"Does the body itself still understand how to preach the Dharma? he asked, and immediately gave him a kick straight to the chest, knocking him down.

He intended to make him get up and become a man of genuine ease and composure. Have you not heard it said: "The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn from gazing at the moon; the elephant has flowers enter its tusks because it was startled by thunder"?

Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Caoshan, “How is it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Caoshan said, “Caoshan is not as good. The monk asked, “And how is it after he appeared in the world?
Caoshan said, “Not as good as Caoshan. The Master said, “To set aside one’s own ground to yield to another is to turn cleverness into clumsiness.
Whether ‘before his appearance’ or ‘after his appearance,’ it is like driving a wedge into empty space. Caoshan has immeasurable offenses. He laughed.
"Your father also has immeasurable transgressions. Can any of you here examine them and find them? One East, two Winter.
[He] crossed his hands at his chest and ascended the hall.
"The river moon shines; the pine wind blows. Throughout the eternal night and clear sky, what is there to do? Blow the unperforated flute upon the clouds."
Externally curved. Among those we meet, those who know me are rare.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "Entering a field of weeds, one does not discriminate; one simply picks whatever grass comes to hand.
The ox of Huaizhou eats the grain; the horse of Yizhou has a bloated belly. Master Zhang, the Administrator of Dushan in Huaining, has cast three cauldrons. Piṇḍola.
The Venerable One did not know where he had lost his lapis lazuli bowl. Tell me, where did it fall? [He] threw down his staff and said:
"It is difficult to deceive the eyes of the assembly.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Before the fifteenth day, it cannot be grasped; after the fifteenth day, it cannot be discarded. It is precisely on the fifteenth."
Day. Striking it, bumping into it; shattered into seven pieces and eight fragments. Even a monk with clear eyes can only grasp a single fragment.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites: Wuzu said, "First enter the gate of Baiyun; next pass the threshold of Baiyun.
This is the chestnut you swallow, this is the non-glutinous rice you eat. If a gentleman should arrive, look well at the skillful means. The Master says: Wuzu...
This old fellow has let his family’s disgrace be broadcast abroad. Yeshan was not like this: "If you can enter the gate of Yeshan, you need not avoid Yeshan’s sword.
Turning over completely beneath the sword, I shall open a single thread for you. As for the fist that strikes the chest—once it has penetrated, there is only a face of raw iron.
Do not be surprised by coarse and meager fare. Skillful means are themselves no skillful means. Entering the Hall:

"A single leaf falls, and the world turns autumnal; a single speck of dust rises, and the great earth is gathered up. All people know this is so; why then do the Buddhas of the three periods not know it?
It is still easy to grasp soil and turn it into gold, but to transform gold back into soil—this is difficult.
It is difficult to turn back.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "When the Buddhas were born, they deserve thirty blows of this staff.
When the Buddhas attained enlightenment, they deserve thirty blows of this staff. When the Buddhas turned the wheel of Dharma, they deserve thirty blows of this staff. Why is that?"
"It is not like this. A crane may have its nine-fold gao, yet it cannot spread its wings; a horse may lack the thousand-li stride, yet it vainly pursues the wind. [He lets out a shout.

Descending from the seat, he invites the administrators and heads of the community to the hall. [He recalls: "Holding up the flower with a smile; standing in the snow to find peace of mind. The Patriarchal Hall shines with glory; the demons..."

With hands clasped in reverence, the fragrance of the lineage continues and the flame is sustained; guest and host interpenetrate, transmitted with absolute clarity without shifting even a single hair’s breadth.
But tell me, for what reason did the Great Sage of Sizhou appear in Yangzhou? "Entering the water, he saw a tall man."
Ascending the hall: When the autumn light is clear and shallow, white dew mingles with the misty isles. How excellent is Avalokiteśvara!

His entire body has entered the wild weeds. It has been clearly explained; whether you understand it or not, it is well. A single arrow pierces the three barriers—lowering your head, where would you seek him?
Please ascend the seat for the Hall discourse. The sun may grow cold; the moon may grow hot. No demons can destroy the True Teaching.
But tell me, what is the True Teaching? The alms bowl becomes damp twice every day.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: When Master Mazu had finished his private instruction, Xitang, Baizhang, and Nanquan were attending him as he gazed at the moon.

The Master asked, "At this very moment, what is it? Xitang said, "It is just right for making offerings. The Master remarked, "This is like looking at plum trees to quench one's thirst. Baizhang said, "It is just right for practicing cultivation. The Master remarked, "Gold does not trade with gold. Nanquan then swept away [the moonlight]. The Master remarked, [this is] "cutting off the flow. The Master then ascended the hall and said: "When the Great Master Mazu finished his private instruction, Xitang, Baizhang, and Nanquan were attending him as they gazed at the moon.

The Master asked, 'At this very moment, how is it? Xitang said, 'It is just right for making offerings. I say: 'This is like looking at plum trees to quench one's thirst. Baizhang said, 'It is just right for practicing cultivation. I say: 'Gold does not trade with gold. Nanquan then swept away [the moonlight]. I say: 'This is cutting off the flow.'"
As he was about to leave, the Master said, "You have only obtained a single peg. Mazu said, "The sutras return to the Canon; Zen returns to the sea.
Only Puyan alone transcends the mundane world. The Master said, "Oṃ mānida li hūṃ phaṭ!
"This one spark has already pierced through your nostrils entirely. Where, then, can you all go to breathe out? He struck his whisk.
Disciples, descend from your seats.
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "Yangqi asked Ciming: 'When the dark birds chirp incessantly and leave the clouds to enter the jumbled peaks—what then?
Ciming said: 'I walk through the wild weeds; you, moreover, enter the deep village. Yangqi said: 'The official does not permit even a needle. Further..."
“Let me ask you a question. Ciming then shouted. Qiji also shouted. Ciming shouted again; Qiji also shouted. Ciming issued two consecutive shouts. Qiji bowed.
The Master said, “These two men are like father and son. It is like playing with a pearl: it does not touch the hand, it does not fall to the ground, and it does not abide in space.
There is nothing mysterious or wondrous about it. How can one even blink an eye here? He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case: Yunmen said, "Awakening to the Way through sound; clarifying the mind through form.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money; letting it go, it turns out to be a steamed bun. Master Yunmen fell down by himself and got up by himself.
Wuzu Fayan, the venerable patriarch, said, "Awakening to the Way through sound; clarifying the mind through form," and then used both hands to beat a drum.
Shi said, "Beng-ba-ra-za—this is a familiar place that is difficult to forget. The Master said, "Yazhou has a living path that I wish to travel together with you all.
He raised his staff and said, "It pierces through the nostrils of everyone; even the lanterns and the pillars find their eyes bulging out.
He struck the ground with the staff and descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "When the entire mandate is held in the main framework, heaven and earth are shrouded in darkness. When one thread is let loose, the Way prospers and the times are peaceful.
But tell me, does the original body, Vairocana, still know shame? Three lives, sixty kalpas.

Ascending the hall, he said: "Since birth, Yefu has been a hundredfold clumsy; when opening his mouth, there is not a single word to say. This morning, pointing at emptiness and painting emptiness, he makes the clear breeze and bright moon laugh to their hearts' content."
Ascending the hall: In every region and every monastery, within the communal groves of the sangha, some flourish while others fall into ruin.

Cutting through iron and severing nails, he topples the Great Statue of Jiazhou and raises up his elder brother Kāśyapa. Take it for granted that the single stream of Cao’an shall remain pure. (He lets out a shout.)
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "A person of empty-headedness speaks empty-headed words and dares to perform empty-headed deeds.

A person of substance speaks only substantial words and performs only substantial deeds. If one were to ask a person of empty-headedness to speak substantial words, they would ultimately never be content;
yet if one asks a person of substance to perform empty-headed deeds, they will ultimately find it unstable. It is just like Master Mazu."
He said, "It is the mind, it is the Buddha; it is not the mind, it is not the Buddha. Then he asked, "Tell me, is this empty? Is it real?
He let out a shout, struck the ground with his staff, and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall to pray for rain: Manifest and majestic in the presence of all, this is the wondrous secret of the divine dragon—toppling mountains and overturning the abysses.
With thunder crashing and lightning flashing, Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the thirty-third heaven, striking the nostrils of Śakra;
when the carp of the Eastern Sea receives a single blow, the rain pours down like an overturned basin, until even Yefu claps his hands and laughs heartily.
Tell me, what is he laughing at? Look after three days.
On the day of the summer retreat’s conclusion, he ascended the hall and held his staff crosswise, saying: "The binding was thus; the unbinding was thus.
When the binding and unbinding are clearly distinguished, everyone has a sudden flash of realization. Yet this very staff refuses to have such a flash. Now tell me, why is that?"
Thus it is: meeting the base, one immediately becomes noble. Leaning on his staff, he descended from the seat.
On the fifteenth day of the ninth month in the first year of the Shaohsi era, special envoys from Yunju and Jianfu arrived together.

He drew lots before the assembly and, having drawn Yunju, he accepted the official notice. Holding it up, he showed it to the assembly and said: "To see it upon the first glance is seeing; to seek it further is difficult."
It comes straight down. Look with urgency! Entering the hall:
"To do it this way is not permitted; not to do it this way is not permitted; to do it both this way and not this way is not permitted at all.
Iron walls and silver mountains are without obstruction. To do it this way is permitted; not to do it this way is permitted; to do it both this way and not this way—[is permitted].
Thus, all is attained. Ten thousand miles of vast sky, a single cloud suddenly surges forth. Where the wheel of the pivot turns, even the masters are still lost.
At the moment of the simultaneous "cracking" and "pecking," one is far, far removed. Today, I cannot help but open a single thread of the Way to reveal a message to you all.
Do you understand? No need to hang up the stone mirror; when dawn breaks, the rooster crows of itself. He further said: "There is the phrase; there is no..."
A phrase: like a vine leaning against a tree; wherever it strikes or brushes against something, there is no room for evasion or retreat. Even the eight-armed Nātha could not hold it back.

The following day, the local military command, acting on the instructions of the Provincial Inspector, sent an official from Lújiāng County to persuade [the Master] to attend the assembly at Jiànfú Monastery.
Holding up the notice, he said: "One does not stop until two; it cannot be grasped, nor can it be let go. Tell me, what is this? After a long silence, he said: "Gōng. (The Official).

The verification is clear. He ascends the hall and says: "Do not seek in the Buddha; do not seek in the Dharma; do not seek in the Sangha. With a solitary boat and short oars, wander freely according to one's nature.
A sudden pivot-turning at the profound gate reveals the transverse and vertical wondrous functions; herein there is no interval whatsoever. Therefore it is said: 'Movement...'"
If one moves like a drifting cloud, one rests like the spirit of a valley. Having no mind for "this" or "that," how could there be any form of coming or going?
Sitting and cutting off a thousand differences, standing like a wall ten thousand fathoms high—do you understand this thoroughly? The great garuḍa spreads its wings, covering the ten regions;
the swallows and sparrows by the fence chirp in vain. Again, he raised the case: Sansheng said, "When I meet people, I come out; but when I come out, I do not act."
Renxue said, "Whenever I meet a person, I do not emerge; when I emerge, I am already a person. These two old fellows were fixated on the one and the two;
they struck the upright with the crooked and used the property of the Sangha as their own private property.
Because of this, the true lineage of Linji has been left unrecoverable down to the present day.
He takes his leave of the assembly: "I am but a simple monk who walks the long path and eats his rice gruel. From south of the Yangtze to north of it, he has shaken heaven and earth;
yet now he follows him away. What need is there to seek the eighth-generation descendant of Yangqi?"
Record of the Discourses at Jianfu Chan Monastery in Rǎozhōu, compiled by the students Gāngmù and others.
Upon entering the monastery, he pointed to the triple gate and said: "The direct path into the gate admits no evasion; whether there be a thousand or ten thousand people, they must face it head-on."
A missed opportunity. Ultimately, where does it land? He lets out a shout.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he says: "If you wish to walk, walk; if you wish to sit, sit. From ancient times until now, it has always been this very thing. He ascends the seat and offers a blessing.
The Master retired. He took his seat. A monk asked: "On the peak of Mount Oufu dwells the deity of peace and happiness; though its divine functions are exhausted, no door can be found to it.
At East Lake, the tiger-subduing [master] has deep karmic ties; shaking hands upon returning, a new smile breaks forth.

I do not ask about the long journey traversed, but what is the single phrase for entering the gate? The Master said: "A thousand chariots share the same ruts. The monk further said: "The assembly has received your grace."

[The monk] departs. The Master says, "Be careful not to miscommunicate this. The monk advances and says, "How can it be helped that the Honorable Prefect sets his heart upon the wondrous Way, and Old Subduer of Tigers has the intention to take charge of this virtue? The Master says, "Cut them off all at once.

The monk says, "When the dragon gains the water, its spirit increases; when the tiger encounters the mountain scenery, its fierce majesty grows. The Master says, "Not yet. Speak further. A monk asks, "What is..."
[The Master] says, "The green mountains layer upon layer within the misty waves. [The student] asks, "From now on, the scenery of Poyang Lake shall be fine;
may the essential core of the patch-robed monk be freely circulated. The Master says, "Six ears do not conspire together. [The student] asks, "What is the person within the realm?
The Master says, "The eyes are horizontal and the nose is straight. [The student] says, "Momo, auspicious qi is added before the hall; it is lush and green."

[The monk] said, "On this pavilion, you surpass all lofty standards. The Master said, "Put it down. The monk stepped forward and asked, "The Master has already granted instruction regarding the person and the environment;
how then is the matter of opening the hall and expounding the Dharma? The Master said, "A high blessing for ten thousand years of spring.
The monk said, "If that is so, then the lineage of Mian will become even more radiant. The Master said, "Where did you see Mian? The monk [remained silent].
[The Master] gave a shout. The Teacher said, "You have missed it behind your head. The Teacher then said: "If you can realize it before words, you have already entered the realm of prolixity;
if you are thoroughly proficient under a phrase, white clouds lie ten thousand miles away. Therefore, it cannot be known by consciousness, nor can it be grasped by intellect.
The whole body comes thus; the whole body abides thus. It spans horizontally across all existence and penetrates vertically through the golden wheel, like a seal impressing upon empty space."
Like a seal impressing clay, like a seal impressing water; every instance conforms to the same track, and its application is without deficiency.

Practicing the Dharma according to the Dharma, the banner of the Dharma is established wherever one goes. Throwing three and releasing two—the intent lies at the tip of the hook. Without establishing any rungs on a ladder, how can one penetrate this thoroughly?

"When the dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, the whole body is revealed; where the Elephant King walks, there is no trace of the fox. (The expression of gratitude is not recorded here. Again, it is said:
Whenever Master Jueyi was asked anything, he would simply raise one finger.
He also said, "At Tianlong, I obtained the 'one-finger Chan,' which I have enjoyed to my heart's content throughout my life. Now tell me, what is this "one-finger Chan"?
He then raised his whisk and asked, "Do you see it? If you can see it, you may walk hand-in-hand with Jueyi. [He then] shed [his robe].
Perhaps not. But Xīnjiànfú could not help but repeat these verses: "One step higher, one step further;
sitting and cutting off the barriers of Buddhas and patriarchs, one loses the path by which they came."
Ascending the hall: Before the fifteenth day, it cannot be grasped; after the fifteenth day, it cannot be relinquished.
Right on the fifteenth day, to grasp it is precisely it; to relinquish it is precisely it. You ask me, and I do not understand at all. Piteous indeed, you only know how to say "Na-si-qi."
Ascending the hall: "At Jianfu Monastery, every activity is a manifestation.
The pillar, the lantern, the triple gate, and the Buddha hall—whether high or low—all blend their light with the dust. Yet at times, they appear with divine heads and ghostly faces.
Where, among you all, will you meet Jianfu? (He lets out a shout.)"

Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Linji addressed the assembly, saying, "I questioned my former teacher three times about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and each time I received sixty blows of the staff, as if they were merely being brushed away with a bundle of mugwort.

Now, if I were to think of receiving another beating, who would be willing to take the first blow? At that moment, a monk came forward and said, "I will take the first blow. Linji took up his staff and passed it to him.
The monk prepared to receive him, and Linji struck him. Xuedou commented: "Linji was perilous in letting go; he was too hasty in pulling back. The Master picked up his staff and said:
"Linji acted according to the mandate, yet he did not realize he had brought shame upon Huangbo.
Xuedou exerts all his strength to carry a wooden board, seeing only one side. But tell me, where does the crux of Jianfu lie?"
He threw down his staff and ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "What is it like when empty space is extinguished? He replied, "The donkey is not a donkey;
the horse is not a horse. He then said, "Heaven cannot cover him; earth cannot support him; empty space cannot contain him; the sun and moon cannot illuminate him. This is...
What manner of style is this? An old rustic knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun; he beats the drum *dong-dong* to sacrifice to the River God. Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example:
A monk asked Yangqi, "Heaven attains the One and becomes clear; Earth attains the One and becomes tranquil. When a patch-robed monk attains the One, what can he do with it?
Yangqi said, "The mouth of the alms bowl points toward heaven. The Master said: "When a patch-robed monk is pressed once, the alms bowl..."
The mouth of the basin is wide. Throughout the world, Yangqi’s disciples look toward the forest to quench their thirst.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The wind does not rustle the twigs; the rain does not break the clods of earth. In five hundred years, a sage appears;
every three thousand years, the Yellow River clears once. This is not for deliberation as Dharma, nor is it for circulation as worldly truth. It is clearly thus."
"What do you say? This too is the lip that has been polished for many days.
He ascended the hall, held his staff crosswise, and said: "Upon this mass of flesh, ten thousand fathoms stand sheer. Entering the mud, entering the water; rocks split and cliffs crumble.
Why is it that everyone fails to understand? After a long silence, he said: "HŪṂ! HŪṂ! He leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year: The New Year begins at dawn; thousands come and ten thousand go, and every single thing is renewed.
Yet, as dust gathers upon the eyes, one must press through the many years within the peach pit; clearly, it is only the person of old.
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival, he held his staff crosswise and said: "The original radiance of the Buddha Dīpaṃkara of the past was like this.
Therefore, from the 'Four Sevens' of India to the 'Two Threes' of the Tang land, the flame was continued and the fragrance linked;
the true wind did not fall. Only Jianfu does not enter this protective society. Why is this so? He struck the ground with his staff and said: "The heavens are vast, the earth is vast."
On the fifteenth day of the second month, he ascended the hall and said: "The Tathāgata has secret words; he buys high and sells low.
Kāśyapa did not conceal them, and this has burdened successive generations. All of you here are descendants of Old Śākyamuni; you live in his house and eat his food.
During the twelve periods of the day and night, how do you make use of it? He struck the seat with his whisk and descended from the hall.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Citing one to clarify the three; words are many, yet the Way is far. The wisdom of all wisdoms is pure;
it is non-dual, without division, without distinction, and without interruption. Now tell me, how does one cite the gate of the Samādhi of the Inexhaustible Treasury? After a long silence, he spoke.
He said, "Those who understand the Dharma are afraid.
He ascended the hall and said: "Dharmatrāta sat facing the wall for nine years; his crime has been caught and exposed. Layman Lu did not know a single character, yet he revealed his true tail.
Monks of the patched-robes school possess a majesty like that of a king; though they have traveled all over the world, it is simply this very thing. Because of this—
It is truly difficult to penetrate. When Fan Kui stepped upon Hongmen, he ascended the hall;
drawing his bow and setting his arrow, it was like a fish swimming in a net. Finding refuge beyond the mundane world, it was like a bird entering a cage.
When life and death are utterly exhausted, it is like a silkworm becoming a cocoon. How can one penetrate these three layers? Old Man Ying’an has exerted all his strength to speak thus. Yet, even so—
This is like handing a ladder to a thief.
When you ascend the hall and can speak from the fullness of your mouth, there is no place of entry;
yet when there is a place of entry, you cannot open your mouth. Tell me, where does the sickness lie? You see only the surging waves, but you do not see the sea dragon.
The Patriarch ascended the hall and said: "Dharma came and faced the wall for nine years; the Second Patriarch stood in the snow until it reached his waist.
Three people took a tortoise and made it into a turtle—a block of dull copper and blunt iron."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "When the faculty does not leave its station, one falls into a sea of poison. Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking of it.
Now tell me, what fault is there in the mountains, rivers, and the great earth? If you can understand this, you may roam horizontally and vertically throughout the land of Japan;
if you do not understand, you shall continue to eat gruel and rice upon the long benches."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and looked over the assembly, saying: "The sword that kills, the blade that gives life; the eyes of Nalaka; the adamantine, true flame.
Clenching the teeth with determination, one’s sincere heart is laid bare in every fragment. That the grass before the Dharma Hall is a fathom deep is not even considered extraordinary.
Ultimately, how can one utter a phrase that penetrates all quarters? After a long silence, he leaned the staff against the wall and descended from the seat.
The twelfth and thirteenth days of the sixth month: the anniversary of the passing of the founding master Ying’an and the late master Mimi. Holding up the incense, he said:
“Leaving home to seek the Way was no easy matter, yet I have run straight into these two old fellows.

One is utterly devoid of human feeling; the other does nothing but snore and mutter in his sleep. They muddle through life like mud and water, wasting their time in vain, living in ruinous indolence and foolishness.”
To strike a blow where there is no settlement is to commit a breach of propriety; to prostrate three times is a regret that can hardly be undone.

Now, reflecting upon this in solitude, it involuntarily provokes a sense of revulsion in others. Therefore, I offer a single stick of incense and brew a cup of tea—not to repay virtue or requite kindness, but merely to engage in a mutual act of deliberate indifference.

Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: where there is release and binding, it is like driving a wedge into empty space; where there is neither release nor binding, one bites into raw iron.
For two thousand years this has been wrongly transmitted, leaving the monks of the world with no place to clear their names. Whether they clear them or not—cliffs collapse and stones shatter.
Ascending the hall: Do not! Do not! The great ocean dries up; Mount Sumeru stands overturned. Moving against the flow, moving with the flow—taking what is mistaken as correct.
Enlightened monks, do not engage in speculative calculation.
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: The Master Zu asked Nanquan, "The mani jewel, people do not recognize it;
they have personally received it within the Tathāgatagarbha. What is this 'garbha'? Nanquan said, "That which comes and goes with you, Old Teacher Wang.
Xuedou added a comment: "A fellow of the weeds. Master Zu asked, "What about when there is no coming or going? Nanquan said, "That too is the garbha."
Xuedou said, "Adding frost to snow. Shizhu asked, "What is the pearl? Master Quan called out, "Shizhu!
Shizhu responded with an "Amen" (a nod). Quan said, "Why do you not understand my words? At that moment, Shizhu attained sudden enlightenment.
Xuedou said, "To perform acrobatics atop a hundred-foot pole is not yet considered perilous; if one can fix a single eye upon this very point, then one is a guest."
By exchanging the host [with the guest], one is able to penetrate deeply into the tiger’s den.

If it were not thus, even if the Master-ancestors had attained enlightenment, it would still be a case of a dragon’s head and a snake’s tail. Master Yuanwu’s verse says: The blue hawk pursues the hare; the black dragon plays with the pearl.

Penetrating the green eyes without blinking, his hand does not miss its mark when illuminating things. Coming and going, yet neither coming nor going—within the weeds, he deceives the Cha-hu. Hundred... [text ends]
"At the tip of the ten-foot pole, one enters the tiger’s den; clearly, the moon rises upon the long coral.
The Master said, "Xuedou provides such a commentary, and Yuanwu offers such a verse. Jianfu also has something to say: 'Clearly, the moon rises upon the long coral.'"
A single scene of splendor illuminates the great void; all sentient beings of the earth share in its enjoyment. Within the Tathāgatagarbha, it has been non-existent from the beginning.

[He ascends the hall, takes up his staff, and strikes the ground, saying: "Mount Sumeru, the waters of the great ocean—all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past have been swallowed up by this very staff.
Now tell me, where shall the lanterns and the pillars find a place to establish themselves?"

[The Master] gave the command: "If you understand, matters are as one family; if you do not understand, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. Relying on his staff, he descended from the seat. The assembly dispersed.

He returned to the hall for the formal discourse. A monk asked: "On the day you departed, the autumn scenery of the lakes and mountains was at its finest; now that you have returned, chrysanthemums fill the eyes."
"Yellow. No one understands the message within this; please, let me proclaim it this very day. The Master said, "From head to tail.
The student asked, "There is a person who is on the road all day long, yet never leaves home. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The heel of his straw sandals has worn through.
The student asked, "There is another person who stays at home all day long, yet never leaves the road. The Master said, "The straw sandals have been lost."
"How is it? The Master said, "The nostrils point toward the heavens. The student asked further, "One day, when the Abbot of Changsha returned from a mountain excursion, he arrived at the gate.
The Head Seat asked him, 'Where have you come from? Changsha replied, 'I have been on a mountain excursion.
What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "He had already seen through him. The Head Seat asked again, "Where did you go? Changsha replied, "Just now I went..."

"The fragrant grasses have gone; they follow the falling flowers back again. [The monk asks: "And what about this? The Master said, "It is vast and boundless above one's head. The monk pressed further:
"The Head Seat says it is very much like the spirit of spring. Shishuang said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping on lotuses.
