The Master said, "Bury them all in a single pit. The monk bowed. He then raised another case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall?"

Yunmen said, "The golden wind is laid bare. The Master picked up his staff and said, "Yunmen may indeed be said to ride the bandit’s horse to pursue the bandit, seize the bandit’s sword to slay the bandit.
Yet you all must not understand it in this way. Why? Because one's life is as precarious as a dangling thread."
[The Master] struck his staff, descended from the seat, and ascended the hall.
"Sometimes when you open your mouth, you may say it correctly, yet you simply do not understand. Other times, even as you open your mouth clearly, you do not say it."
Again, he alone nodded his head. Now tell me, which one did he save? He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall, he raised an ancient case: "When Baizhang returned from accompanying Mazu on a mountain excursion, he suddenly wept.
His colleagues asked him, 'Are you missing your parents? Baizhang said, 'Nothing. They asked, 'Were you scolded by someone? Baizhang said, 'Nothing. They asked, 'Why are you weeping?'"
Baizhang said, "Go ask the Abbot. The attendant went to ask Mazu, who said, "You go ask him yourself.
When the attendant returned to his quarters, he saw Baizhang laughing heartily. The attendant asked, "Just now you were crying;
why are you laughing now? Baizhang replied, "Just now I was crying; now I am laughing. The attendant was left bewildered. The Master said, "At that time..."
If at that time one were to encounter a stubborn blockhead, even Baizhang and Mazu would have to retreat.
Later, Dahui wrote a verse: "Sometimes laughing, sometimes weeping; sorrow and joy intermingle, urging on in secret. How can this principle be brought forward to others?
To mend a broken string, one must use phoenix glue. The Master said, "Master Dahui possessed a truly magnificent spirit and character."
It is like facing an ancient toward their back with hands clasped. Jianfu also has one verse: "Weeping does not reach the end; laughing does not reach the end.
I turn my belly inside out and empty my guts to tell you: father and son are not kin—knowing or not knowing, lift up your head: three catties of iron behind it."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example. He cited Xuan Sha’s instruction to the assembly: "I constantly place you all upon the crown of my head;
I dare not err with you by even a hair's breadth. The Master said, "Xuan Sha speaking thus was very much like knowingly committing an offense.
Why? Even before he had laid hand or foot upon them, they were already being buried; how much more so when he places them upon the crown of his head?"
[The Master] ascends the hall. Although it is thus, those who have not undergone the hardships of practice do not know this.
He ascends the hall, strikes the meditation staff, and says: "It settles heaven and earth; it resolves hesitation. It is the spark struck from flint, the flash of lightning.

Guest and host are clearly distinguished; it stands like a wall ten thousand fathoms high. Were it not for one who possesses the penetrating Dharma-eye and hangs the talisman behind the elbow, they would often be right in front of it and yet miss it."
A missed opportunity. But tell me, what serves as the proof? He then threw down his staff and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised the following case: Xinghua addressed the assembly, saying, "Today, there is no need for 'thus' or 'what if.
I ask you simply to enter directly with a single blade; Xinghua will serve as witness for all of you. At that time, the Elder Minde came forward and bowed. As he rose—
Minde shouted. Huaxia also shouted. Minde shouted again. Huaxia also shouted. Minde bowed and returned to the assembly.
Huaxia said, "Elder Minde has today been measured against Huaxia’s thirty blows. Had it been anyone else, not even a single blow could have been compared."

"Why is that? It is because he understood the single shout not as the function of a single shout. The Master said: "Xinghua invited the thief to ruin the house; Minde seized him by the hair and brought him to the yamen.
Yet you further say he understood the single shout not as the function of a single shout; you do not realize how you are insulting the majestic style of our Linji school.
Have you not heard it said: 'The master does not wait for the pecking and the hatching; when pecking and hatching occur simultaneously, both are lost'?"
Returning from his travels outside the district, he ascended the hall and said: "The ancients said, 'If mugwort grows among hemp, it will never be straight.
For a monk to leave the pure assembly is most unreasonable. I, this mountain monk, have separated myself from the great assembly for over a month;
I did not realize I was dragging mud and water along with me. Tell me, how thick is my face? He continued: "The people of Yin used cypress; the people of Zhou used chestnuts."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the case]: Xuedou said, "The spring mountains layer upon layer of wild green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure.

Vast and silent between heaven and earth, standing alone, what can one gaze upon to the limit? The Master shouted, "The great Xuedou, it seems, did not realize his four corners had collapsed to the ground!
Nevertheless, when the road is long, one knows the horse's strength; when affairs have endured, one sees the person's heart."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Panshan said, "It is like throwing a sword into the air; one cannot discuss whether it reaches its mark or not.

This is because the wheel of emptiness leaves no trace, and the blade of the sword remains unimpaired. The Master said, "At such a moment, how is it? Even those with hearts and livers of iron would break their guts.
Ascending the hall, he raised this case: A monk asked Mazu Daoshi, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master said, "Come closer; I will tell you. As the monk stepped forward, the Master struck him across the face with his palm and said, "Six ears do not share a secret.
Master Nanyuan Huanglong commented: "If even the ancients said that six ears do not share a secret, how much less could two hundred and three [ears] do so?"
A hundred vast debates—calamity! Calamity! When Jianfu looks at it, it is truly laughable. But tell me, what is there to laugh at?
The thief has no seed; they merely deceive one another.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The moon arises as one: a decree from the Son of Heaven within the universe. The moon arises as two: face-to-face, there is no place to hide.
The moon arises as three: the lanterns and the pillars let loose their foolishness, startling the people of Silla and Campā to clash foreheads.
You all, thirty years hence, must take care not to forget this!"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Yantou, "What is it like when arising and ceasing never cease? Yantou shouted, "Who is it that arises and ceases?
The Master said, "Because the ancients were compassionate, they had such talk that 'fell into the weeds. Jianfu, however, is not like this."
Suddenly, [a monk] asked, "What is it like when arising and ceasing do not stop? The Master simply gave him a shout.
Ascending the hall, he raised his whisk and said, "Master Zhao said: 'Heaven and earth share the same root as I; the myriad things are one body with me.
[The Master] struck the meditation seat once with the whisk and said, 'Do you all feel any pain or itchiness? If you do not...'"
If you perceive it, you betray this mountain monk; if you perceive it, you bury yourself. To speak clearly in this manner is like a turtle walking on land.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The root of sentient beings relies upon the ocean of wisdom as its source; the stream of conscious beings takes the Dharma-body as their essence.
Raising his whisk, he said: "This is not the Dharma-body. Speech and silence, movement and stillness, are not the Dharma-body.
The myriad phenomena in their dense array are not the Dharma-body. Now tell me, what do you call the essence? With the whisk, he struck [the floor].
The Zen master said: "Sixty kalpas in three lifetimes.
A letter from Master Yong of Baiting at Guifeng arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "On the sea, the aged Baiting races with all;
He deeply detests Buddhas and Patriarchs for harboring eternal ignorance. Suddenly, he executes a somersault turn; Once again, the single stream of Longmen flows clear."

Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: What is the precedent for this "dissolution of the regulations" today? A horse’s face and a donkey’s muzzle—emptiness of mind is the passing of the imperial examination.

Two thousand years ago, the Old Man with the Yellow Face spoke words of empty liberation; walking in the dark, one is neither aware nor knows it, so let there be as much laughter and wonder as you please.
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Double Festival (Chóngmíng Jié): The Buddha-body is unconditioned and does not fall within the realm of numerical categories;

the Buddha’s marks are markless, yet their manifestation is solemn and majestic. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth emit various kinds of light; grasses, trees, insects, and animals manifest extraordinary and sublime events.

For this reason, the Divine Palace descends with celebration and the True Lord is born. The loyal hearts of ten thousand nations are turned toward him, offering prayers for the sagely longevity of the One Man. At the seat of authority, there is...
The Way: the various schools align toward the central source. A single phrase is without partiality; its spiritual radiance shines through with clarity. Do you understand this fully?
It is the assembly of merit adorned by pure wisdom. May the sacred personage endure for ten million myriad years.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example. He said: "Muzhou addressed the assembly, saying: 'To tear it open is up to me; to fold it back together is up to me.
At that time, a monk came forward and asked: 'What is tearing it open? Muzhou said: 'Three times nine is twenty-seven;
bodhi and nirvana; suchness and liberation; this very mind is Buddha. I simply do so; what about you? The monk said, "I..."
"Not so," said the Master. Zhou said, "The cup falls to the ground; the saucer shatters into seven pieces. The Master said, "This too is laughable.
Great as he was, Master Muzhou was squeezed by this monk until he was like a crab falling into boiling water—every hand and foot exposed all at once."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: One day, while Nanquan was cutting thatch, a monk asked him, "Where does the road to Nanquan lead?
Nanquan held up his sickle and said, "This was bought for thirty coins. The monk said, "I am not asking about this;
where does the road to Nanquan lead? Nanquan replied, "It serves me well. The Master said, "Nanquan..."
The living path before Master Nanquan’s gate is opened wide in eight characters. This monk, though clever within, feigns deafness and dumbness.
Had he seen Nanquan say at that moment, "I have used it with such speed," and immediately turned a step back, saying, "You’ve tricked me!"—even the great and small Nanquans would have had to retreat.
Ascending the hall: Looking up, one does not see the sky; looking down, one does not see the earth. Having finished eating, one eats sleep. This is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths.
Ascending the hall: He cited Yunmen, who said: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money. When he lets go of his hand, it is originally..."
"Come! This is a steamed bun. The Master said, "A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech.
He ascended the hall and said: "All obstacles are ultimate enlightenment; whether mindfulness is attained or lost, there is nothing that is not liberation.
Śākyamuni Buddha bared his heart and exposed his gall, cutting off all currents, yet he was still not free from his own underlying view. To this day, it remains unresolved."
If one person can examine it thoroughly, even if they can examine it thoroughly, it is still "Dou Ba’s Cloth Shirt.
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "Muzhou addressed the assembly, saying: 'I see that Baizhang does not know good from bad. As soon as the great assembly had gathered..."
With his staff, he drove them all down at once. He then called out to the assembly; the assembly turned their heads back.
The Staff Master said: "What is this? There is no place for conversation here. When Master Huangbo’s assembly had just gathered, he likewise drove them all down at once with his staff.
He then called out to the assembly; the assembly turned their heads back. Huangbo said: "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain and much wind—it is still somewhat better than that."
Xuedou said, "To speak of it as 'still leaving something to be desired'—it is simply not yet there. According to Xuedou, he would have used his staff to drive them off and left it at that.

Among those present was one who possessed a "spearheadless iron hammer," well able to shoulder the burden, capable of encompassing past and present, and able to cut off heaven and earth in a single stroke.
He then took up his staff and said, "I let this one move. The Master said, "The more you look, the more you see."
Nonsense! These old fellows have come out to set up their nets and spread their snares, yet they are merely scooping clams and catching shrimp on level ground.
Little do they realize that while they exhaust their own minds, they only end up making others laugh until their mouths split. *Duh!* (A blow!)
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra fall headlong east and west; mud-pigs and scabby dogs form a pack and a troop.
They pull out the nostrils of Old Śākyamuni, so that Śakra Devendra awakens in his dreams and, without realizing it, claps his hands and laughs aloud.
Tell me, what kind of realm is this? Let those with eyes discern it."
Master Xie Zhi shangtang: Releasing both and gathering both at once—the eyes cannot deceive. With empty hands, he fully upholds [the Way]; who is his true confidant?
Thus, like voices responding to one another and spirits seeking out their kin, his entire being comes forth in this way, and his entire being abides thus.
Although it is so, tell me: how do you express the single phrase "the wind is calm and the waves are still"? The *San-tai* must be...
Everyone is urging me.
Ascending the hall for the Lantern Festival: Today is the fifteenth day of the first month; let us raise an old koan. One lamp, a hundred thousand lamps;
a thousand people, ten thousand people look on. At the tips of the hundred grasses, beyond the limit of time—should you meet someone who is one of these "insiders," it will ultimately...
"Not turning according to the shifting shadows of others.
He ascended the hall and said: "Vimalakīrti said, 'Those who give to you do not call you a field of merit; those who make offerings to you fall into the three evil realms. The Master said:
'Do you still see Vimalakīrti’s heart, liver, and five internal organs? When one moves a flower, the butterflies arrive with it; when one buys a stone... "
Obtaining abundant clouds.
The Dharma Master is sent up to the hall: "Of the ten thousand households and a thousand gates, those who arrive are rare; one push and one shove depend on the moment.
This true message beyond the limit of Vipaśyin—unless you are a true connoisseur, do not let others know it. If you do indeed know it, then cast it aside."
"Three releases and two [restraints]. Regardless of high or low, gather them all up with full intent and carry them home along with the moon.

He ascended the hall and said: "Lanxi said: 'If one discusses this matter, it is like a great bell waiting to be struck; the sound responds to the vast sky. It is like a precious mirror facing the courtyard;
its reflection encompasses the myriad phenomena. He also said: 'If one discusses this matter, what need is there to mention Nāgārjuna or Aśvaghoṣa?'"
Devadatta Śāriputra’s eloquence was like a cascading torrent and his wisdom like flowing water; none were able to fathom him. The Master said:
"Langya’s such revealing is also like selling private salt on the public highway."

Tell me, where does the meaning lie? One might think it is the red beard, yet there is also the red-bearded man.
Entering the hall: "Today is the twentieth day of the ninth month; do not be surprised that time passes as swiftly as lightning. Travelers come and go from south to north in constant throngs."

He ascended the hall and said, citing a case: A monk asked Fenzhou, "What is the phrase for receiving a beginner? Fenzhou said, "You are traveling on pilgrimage."
A monk asked, "What is the phrase for discerning a patch-robed monk? Zhaozhou said, "The sun rises in the west at dawn.

"If you cannot grasp it, you will lose the benefit of Jianfu.

He ascended the hall and said, citing the case: "When Master Liang-sui first visited Magu, as soon as Magu saw him coming, he took up a hoe and went to weed the grass, paying no attention to him at all.

"Know it! Liang-sui knows where it is; others do not. Yunmen said, "There is immediately a wave against the current. The Master said, "To act for others must be thorough;

Ascending the hall: Shigong draws his bow; Luzu faces the wall. The true command is not being carried out; he twists the crooked to make it straight.

The Buddha’s Birthday; ascending the hall: "Today is the eighth day of the fourth month; everywhere they bathe the Buddha.

Sitting on the road. The bridge flows, but the water does not flow.

He then said, "A-he-he! There is nothing to compare it with; how can I be told what to say? He struck the meditation staff and descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall: For five years here, I have idly followed conditions; with no fixed mind regarding going or staying, I am naturally at ease.
In the sixth month, fine auspicious snow falls in drifts; you must know that this is a distinct world within a single pot.
Record of the Sayings of Chan Master Zhidu of Xiangshan in Mingzhou, compiled by the students Shenkai and others.

"Chen. The Master said, "Dharma Teacher Shui has thrown a brick to draw out a jade; one does not know whether he has instead obtained a mere brick.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Sometimes they sit in meditation in a daze; sometimes they are constantly making a commotion.
For years now, these traveling monks have all had this same ailment. I tell you: stop making a commotion! Upon entering the gate, cast off this entire body;
then, in every instance, there is the handling of a live snake."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following] case: Wuzu said, "Four or five hundred *shí* of wheat, two or three thousand *luó* of rice—what a wonderful recipe for abstaining from grain!

Xiangshan has a skillful means that he wishes all people to know together: to penetrate the diamond circle and chew the iron delicacy finely;
once satiated, one forgets a hundred hungers, and only then will you believe that we have not deceived one another.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient precedent, saying: "An ancient worthy said: 'Poverty last year was not yet poverty; poverty this year is true poverty.

After returning from a military expedition in Western Zhejiang, he ascended the hall and gave this discourse. He cited a case: A monk asked Master Suxi, "What is the Buddha Dingguang?
Suxi said, "A duck swallows a snail. The monk asked, "Does this allow the student to turn himself around? Suxi said, "The eyes."

The Master said: "A duck swallowing a snail—how utterly decisive! But tell me, what does 'running south and rushing north' actually accomplish?"
“Matters of the borderlands: plowing fields to earn a meal; I recall Old Yangqi all over again. He ascended the hall and said, citing Dahui:
“Where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; an iron scale-weight is being eaten by worms. Where there is no Buddha, run past quickly;
you bump into the broken stove at Mount Songshan. Even if you meet someone three thousand miles away, do not speak with them.”
A mistaken citation: "Two stone people whispering to each other. If that is so, then one does not go. These words have already circulated throughout the world:
"Picking the willow flowers, picking the willow flowers. Oṃ ma ni da li hūṃ phaṭ. The Master said:
"The Elder Dahui exerted his full strength, yet he could only reach this point. Do you know where Xiangshan falls? The iron mountain collapses."
Overturning the Silver Mountain. The platter turns the pearl, and the pearl rolls upon the platter. Intimately embroidering the mandarin ducks at leisure, the golden needle is never shown to others.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Zhaozhou visited Linji. Just as Zhaozhou had washed his feet, Linji came down and asked, "What is..."

Baizhang said, "If you understand, then understand; why do you keep at me like a greedy eater? Linji shook his sleeves and departed.

Baizhang said, "After thirty years of traveling as a mendicant, today you have wrongly provided a commentary for others. The Master said: "Half rain, half sun; peach blossoms red, pear blossoms white. He added a dot.
He put it on and went away; there was no need for further chewing or pecking. What is the place where he wrongly added his footnote? Try to say it. Ascending the hall, he raised the case:
Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "What is the Way? Nanquan said, "The ordinary mind is the Way. Zhaozhou said, "Can one still direct oneself toward it?
Nanquan said, "To intend to direct yourself toward it is already to deviate. Zhaozhou said, "If one does not intend, how can one know it is?"
Dàowén said, "The Way does not belong to knowing, nor does it belong to not-knowing. Knowing is deluded awareness; not-knowing is neutral ignorance (*avyākṛta*).
If one truly penetrates the Way beyond doubt, it is as vast and open as the great void; how could one forcibly impose right and wrong? At this, Zhāozhōu suddenly attained great enlightenment.
The Master said, "Under the clear blue sky and bright sun, what have you awakened to? *Du!* *Du!* *Du!* The pearl of the dragon has been shattered!"
At Canglong Cave, he ascended the hall and said: "A monk asked Mingzhao, 'Among the seven cubs born to a tiger, which one has no tail? Zhao replied, 'The seventh one has no tail.
The Master said: 'The seventh one has no tail; he does not fall into the ranks of the common herd, but alone reveals his claws and fangs."
If you direct your mind toward it, you will ultimately find it difficult to see; you must believe that a lotus blooms within the fire.
Ascending the hall, he held his staff horizontally and said: "In stillness there is a vast clamor; amidst clamor there is profound stillness.
The bell tolls as the moon grows dark; the stream flows as the fifth watch begins. The staff, however, is vexed; what a pity for this fine time—wasted in triviality."
[The time] has passed in vain. Relying on my staff, I descend from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised [the case]: "Dharma Flower addressed the assembly, saying: 'If one does not seal the Vairocana, how can one propagate the mind of the ancient Buddha?
The bright moon shines upon the secluded valley; the cold waves resound like the sound of a night mortar. Today, Layman Jian’an has arrived; I, this mountain monk, likewise have [something to say]."
A single verse: Seated, he cuts off the summit of Vairocana; transcendent, he spans past and present. All myriad conditions are stripped away; it is but a single piece of the Patriarch’s mind.
The Master accepted the invitation from Tiger Hill in Pingjiang Prefecture and held up the ceremonial document, saying: "Of the ancients and the moderns, those who share the Way know. One.

He ascended the hall. A monk asked, "When a master does not wait for the 'cracking' and the 'pecking,' but loses the moment when the cracking and pecking occur simultaneously—how is this?
He replied, "Once a single character enters the gates of officialdom, even nine oxen cannot pull the cart out. He then said, "In the kingdom of Magadha, he personally issued this edict. Small...

When the Master entered the monastery, he pointed to the main gate and said: "The single phrase upon entering the gate: guest and host are clearly distinguished; no need to snap one's fingers—the heavens [open]."

The Master said, "The sword has long since departed. [The student] asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master held up his whisk.
[The student] asked, "What is the guest within the host? The Master struck the meditation seat once. [The student] asked, "What is..."
"This is the master among masters. The Master said, "Apprehend it before the sound. The student asked, "What is the guest within the guest?

The Master said, "Sifting soil and scattering dust. The student asked, "When host and guest are clearly distinct, with no partiality toward one or the other, who can know the secret message within the jar?"
The Master said, "Torn asunder. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "The single aperture above has been opened wide; one sits beyond the limit of Vipaśyin Buddha, severing all boundaries.
Flowing forth from within one’s own breast, its application is without error. Every point accords with the path; it penetrates sound and form, transcending both sight and hearing.
It is not something known by the Three Sages or Ten Saints, nor can it be fathomed by supernatural powers or transformations."

Unconcerned with gain or loss, not failing to respond to the immediate occasion, and not treading in the footsteps of predecessors—how can one raise the cry? The Buddhas of the three periods of time have only said that it must be known by oneself;
the patriarchs of successive generations have been unable to lift it up entirely. It truly shines upon heaven and reflects upon earth, changing the constellations and shifting the stars.
When a true master encounters another, they merely blink an eye. Therefore it is said: "The path leading upward is where not even a thousand sages have passed."

The Tradition: never having been personally approached, we have long been separated by the great trichiliocosm. At such a time as this, how shall one reveal the single phrase of the "Direct Presence"?

He then ascended the hall and, citing a precedent, said: "Master Lingguan used to sit with his door closed. One day, Xuefeng knocked on the door, and Lingguan opened it immediately."
[The Master] entered the gate. Xuefeng grabbed him and said, "Are you a commoner or a sage? Guo'an spat at him and said, "This wild fox spirit! He pushed the door open, then closed it again.
Xuefeng said, "I must also recognize my elder brother. The Master said, "If one does not do the first, one will not rest until the second.
There is a reason for the mutual exchange of guest and host. A scorched brick strikes the frozen ground to its very core; a bloodshot eye collides with a firebrand."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "A phrase, no phrase—like a vine leaning against a tree. Meng Baba goes right along like this.
He then struck the meditation seat and said: "Suru suru!"

One flower opens into five petals; the fruition is naturally accomplished. The Master says: "Wang Xizhi’s calligraphy penetrates the stone by three inches. Li Bai and Du Fu..."
This composition possesses a brilliance of ten thousand fathoms. It is indeed so; yet those who succeed are few, while those who fail are many.

When the great function manifests before us, how can one discern it? Guishan said, "Wrong. Yangshan turned his head and said, "The junior Dharma brother Xiangyan has arrived;
do not say he was silent. The Master said, "If it is, it is entirely so; if it is not, it is entirely not. When the great function manifests before us..."
Walking hand in hand, we return together; yet one does not know that they still traverse the realms of separation and non-separation.
Entering the hall, he raised an anecdote: A monk asked Master Wenshu of Dingzhou, "All dharmas return to the One;

where does the One return? Wenshu said, "The Yellow River has nine bends. Muguan’s verse says: "How can the nine bends be viewed even with a sidelong glance? Who understands how to steer the boat apart from the waves?"
Lan: "Once Mañjuśrī unfurled his 'heaven-turning hand,' it was as if the ten thousand tributary streams were all made to flow toward the sea. The Master said:
"If Wumuan Zen Master speaks thus, he possesses only one eye."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Dharma came for nine years facing the wall; he searched for it but could not find it. The Second Patriarch stood prostrating himself, forcing himself to be alert.
When has he ever dreamed of the stinking sweat of a patch-robed monk? Have you all yet awakened sharply? He let out a shout.
The Master traveled abroad for the sake of seeking teachings and returned home. Addressing the assembly, he said, "An enlightened-eyed monk has lost his nostrils;
there is a thief, yet no stolen goods.
He ascended the hall and cited the following: When Linji was in Huangbo’s hall dozing off, Huangbo came down and saw him, and with his staff...
He struck the wooden board once. Linji raised his head; seeing it was Huangbo, he went back to sleep.
Huangbo struck the board once again, then went up to the upper room where he saw the Head Seat meditating.
He said, "The junior monk in the lower room is actually meditating, while you here are indulging in idle thoughts. He struck the board once more and departed. The Master said:
Beating sleep while sitting in meditation; sitting in meditation while beating sleep. Whether there is gain or loss, one does not leave the marketplace.
Old Huangbo was truly foolish and deluded; deep plowing with shallow sowing is known by few.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Regarding the saying, 'The phrase exists and the phrase does not exist, like a vine leaning against a tree'—what does this mean? The Master replied, "A scale-weight dipped in vinegar.
The monk pressed further, "When the tree falls and the vine withers, what then? The Master replied, "Changing the bones and washing the entrails; walking alone under the open sky."
Jin said, "Tangshan laughed loudly, 'he-he. How else can one discuss this? He replied, "The sword that kills, the blade that gives life.
Then he said, "All of you eat your meals all day long, yet you have never bitten into a single grain of rice;
you wear your clothes all day long, yet you have never hung on a single thread of silk. Xiu of Huqiu grants you a point of entry, but as for you all—"*
All day long he eats rice, yet he has never bitten into a single grain; all day long he wears clothes, yet he has never been touched by a single thread.
He cannot help but be like a blind donkey following the great crowd. Do you know how Huqiu enters the mud and enters the water?
Thirty years hence...

On the twenty-second day of the fifth month in the third year of the Qingyuan era, he reverently received the imperial decree to serve as the abbot of Lingyin Chan Temple in Jingde, Lin’an Prefecture. The Master led the assembly to face the palace gate to express their gratitude for the imperial favor. He held up...
The Imperial Edict was presented to the assembly, saying: "The news from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa has descended from the Nine Palaces as a single segment of radiant light.
It is like ten suns shining together; the myriad spirits look up in reverence, and a wind arises across the hundred valleys. The proof is before your very eyes—everyone, realize it!"
The preface states: "This is a settled case; it is known even before it is raised. Without touching the tip of a hair, it reveals the True Dharma Eye.
Should there still be lingering attachment to viewing and listening, please allow me to expound upon it."

Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "The reputation of the Way has been heard afar, reaching unto the heavens; imperial grace now arrives from the side of the sun. The fourfold assembly looks up in reverence;
we pray to hear the prayers for the Emperor. The Master said:
"The ten-thousand-year pine of Mount Nanyue. The monk stepped forward and said: "With these words, the longevity of the South Mountain has already been prayed for; throughout the eight directions..."
"I congratulate you on this great peace," [the student] said. The Master replied, "The heavens are vast, the earth is vast.

[The student] asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master replied, "A broken oil lamp. [The student] asked, "What is the second phrase? The Master replied, "Tearing asunder empty space. [The student] asked, "What is the third phrase?
The Master replied, "Chopping nails and cutting iron. [The student] remarked, "Even if one splits apart Mount Hua, the thunder is not yet swift."
"The moon illuminating the vast ocean is not its light. The Master said, "That too is commonplace. The student asked, "A monk asked Baizhang, 'What is the extraordinary matter?
Baizhang replied, 'Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The talk has fallen away."
The monk stepped forward and asked, "I do not yet understand where you saw Baizhang. The Master held up his whisk and said, "Do you see it?
The monk replied, "Not only does the Sun of the Buddha shine once more, but the monastic community also has cause for reliance. The Master said, "You have simply missed Baizhang.
The monk bowed, and the Master then said, "The Heart-Seal of the Patriarchs is like the mechanism of an iron ox; if one moves toward it..."
Seal it and abide; abiding, it is immediately broken by the seal. If one neither departs nor abides, the total functioning of the great utility shines forth everywhere.
Pure light overflows the eyes, penetrating through past and present, manifesting the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye and transmitting the heart-essence of the Buddhas and Patriarchs.
The wondrous function extends vertically and horizontally; at every turn, all paths converge. Truly, under the sky of Yao and the sun of Shun, all share in the joy of peace and prosperity.
With bellies drummed and songs sung, they return home to sit in stability. But tell me, how do you express the single phrase of "Facing the Sun"?

The heavens are high and the myriad forms are upright; the seas are vast and the hundred rivers flow toward them. Again, he raised the example: Sansheng said, "Whenever I meet someone, I come forth; yet when I come forth, I do not act for their sake."
Renxue said, "When I meet a person, I do not come out; when I come out, I am already that person. The Master [Zhaozhou] took up the case and said:
"These two old fellows extinguished the True Dharma Eye of Linji, yet they went hand-in-hand along the road to Chang'an.
Even until now, they have continued to obstruct one another. But what is this 'going hand-in-hand' phrase? It is like pulling open the lock of the golden hall and crashing through it."

On the fifth day of the sixth month in the third year of the Qingyuan era, he entered the temple. Pointing to the triple-gate, he said: "The single path of Vulture Peak has been reached by those who have attained realization."
Still lost in confusion, with no steps established, upon whom can one rely to set foot? When we finally meet face-to-face, there is nothing more to do:
beneath the moon, we part the clouds and let out a single cry.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "If you wish to walk, you walk; if you wish to sit, you sit. As the water rises, the boat floats higher; as the mud thickens, the Buddha grows larger."
Ascending the seat, he held up the incense and said:

"This one offering of incense is respectfully offered to extend the boundless life-span of the present Emperor—ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Ten thousand ten thousand years! He then held up the incense again and said:
"This one incense offering is respectfully presented for the Chancellor, Duke of the State, and all the civil and military officials of the court, to augment their years of service and longevity.

Next, he held up the incense and said: "This incense is burned within the burner as an offering to the late Great Master Mian, who previously resided at this mountain and later resided at Tiantong, in order to repay the milk of the Dharma. He then took his seat. A monk asked: "The drum sounds—"
"The bell tolls as we discuss the true nature of reality; the lanterns and pillars emit rays of light. There is no need to seek the road to Chang’an any further;
you have already entered the imperial capital with your whole being. A student stepped forward and requested, "I ask the Master to answer my question. The Master held up his whisk and said:
"Do you see it yet? The student replied, "This very dwelling in the mountains is unintentional; even the past attainment of Buddhahood was without mind. The Master said, "He has followed along.
The student said, "In the past, Zen Master Yuanwu addressed the assembly, saying: 'There is one person who does not leave their home, yet is always on the road.
There is another person who is always on the road, yet does not leave their home. What is the meaning of this?"
"How so? The Master said, "The eight-sided staff in the hand of Vajrapāṇi. The student asked, "Today the Master was at home; were you on the way?
The Master said, "Śāriputra’s supernatural powers could do nothing about it. The student said, "In that case, today we have the joy of the master returning home.
The Master said, "All at once, he cut them off entirely. The student said, "In the past, when Attendant Wang visited Linji..."
Question: “A fine assembly of monks—do they study the scriptures, or do they practice seated meditation? Jie said, “They do not study the scriptures;
they do not practice seated meditation. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, “An unperforated iron hammer. [The student] further asked: “The Attendant said, ‘Ultimately, what are they doing?
Jie said, ‘I teach them all to become Buddhas and Patriarchs. What about that? The Master said, “Shame! Shame!”
The monk bowed in shame. He stepped forward and said, "Even at this very moment, Lingyin has a fine assembly of monks.
I wonder, what kind of monks are they? The Master said, "Feel free to speculate. The monk bowed.

The Master then said, "As for this matter, it cannot be known through a mind that seeks, nor can it be attained by a mind that strives for non-attainment; it cannot be constructed through words, nor can it be found in silence."
Silent penetration: Great wisdom is profoundly clear; a thousand differences are cut off at once. The great capacity responds perfectly; every point is fully revealed.

Therefore, the Buddhas appear in the world for this one great causal matter; the Patriarchs come from the West to point directly to the human mind, so that by seeing one's nature, one becomes a Buddha.
Thus, the numinous light shines through, universally extolling the Imperial House; the ten thousand nations rejoice in heart, together pouring forth their devotion to the Sage.

[The Master] said: "Furthermore, regarding the phrase 'knowing gratitude and repaying kindness'—how do you speak it? One person sits upright in non-action, and throughout the world the five-petaled flower blooms.

(Having finished expressing his thanks. He then raised another case: One day, when the World-Honored One ascended the seat and had just adjusted his robes, Mañjuśrī struck the gavel and said, "Behold clearly the Dharma of the Dharma-King;
such is the Dharma of the Dharma-King. Thereupon, the World-Honored One descended from the seat. The Master [said]: ...
Holding up the whisk, he said: "The Samādhi of the World-Honored One and the Samādhi of Mañjuśrī are both upon the tip of this whisk.
Do you all see it? As soon as the dragon from the deep springs stirs, the vermilion phoenix soars aloft."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Baling, "Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different?
Baling replied, "When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it goes down into the water. Master Baiyun said, "Baling only managed to say half of it.

Baiyun would not put it this way: 'Scoop up the water and the moon is in your hand; play with the flowers and their fragrance fills your robes. The Master commented: "Baiyun exerted his full strength."
The Way—this can only be spoken of as eighty percent. When asked about Lingyin, he simply said to him: "Humanity, self, ignorance—all pierced by a single spit.
Entering the hall, he said: "Heaven does not speak, yet the four seasons proceed; Earth does not speak, yet the myriad things grow. The staff does not speak, yet the Buddha..."
The Patriarch’s example: have you all, during these one hundred and twenty days, ever even dreamed of it?
Where Yu’s strength could not reach, the sound of the river flows toward the west.
On the anniversary of the passing of my late teacher Mimi, I offer incense: Baizhang was deaf; Huangbo stuck out his tongue.
The descendants of later generations are half-born and half-extinguished. The broken sandpot once leaked its secret; in the sixth month of midsummer, frost and snow fall from the blazing sky.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised an example: Xuefeng held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "This staff of mine is intended only for those of middling and inferior capacity.
At that time, a monk came forward and asked, "What if a person of superior capacity were to arrive? Xuefeng threw the staff down.
Later, Yunmen said, "I do not engage in the same entanglements as Xuefeng. He suddenly took up his staff and said, "This one of mine is intended only for those of middling or inferior capacity.
A monk asked, "What if a person of superior capacity should suddenly arrive?

Yunmen struck him with the staff. The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "The great capacity responds perfectly; the great function is direct and immediate. Xuefeng and Yunmen obtained only a single fragment. Thus it concludes.
In the end, what is it? Not saying. Not saying. He ascended the hall.
Looking up, one does not see the sky; looking down, one does not see the earth. The eyebrows are above the eyes; the breath exits from within the nostrils.
Under my school of patch-robed monks, such a person deserves a severe blow of the staff. Why is this so? It is easy to distinguish the snow.
[The Master] scatters flour; it is difficult to distinguish the soot within the ink.

He lets out a shout. Then he ascends the hall and cites the following: When Muzhou saw a monk coming to visit him, he immediately shouted and said, "Venerable sir, why are you stealing the monastery's snacks?
The monk said, "I have only just arrived; why do you say I am stealing the monastery's snacks? Muzhou replied, "The stolen goods are right here!"
"Indeed. The Master’s verse says: "The treasures of the jewel mountain are exhausted; The whole body enters the wild weeds.
If you are a phoenix chick, You will not seek them there."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are but the clarity of one's nature. Fundamentally, there is no person who is deluded or awakened;
it simply requires realization today. He struck the meditation seat once and said: "Realization today! The long month has thirty days; the short month has twenty-nine."
Ascending the hall: At Lingyin, the furnace is opened, yet there is not a single spark of fire. Taking what is non-existent to be existent—who can distinguish the refined from the coarse?
Should you hesitate or deliberate, the black staff shall split your spine and tear through your ribs; let every one of you be left with a mouthful of ashes.

Returning from his travels, he ascended the hall. Moving eastward to the west, moving westward to the east—the host within the guest, the guest within the host. The entire great earth is fully encompassed;
a thousand differences are raised at once. "Strike the drum and all are invited to look!"—the whole body is nothing but mud.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A thousand people crowding the gate are not as good as one person stepping through the pass.

Once one person steps through the pass, there is no doubt that a thousand or ten thousand people will all reach the ground of peace and bliss. Having reported this to you thus, is there anyone who does not find it agreeable? After a long silence.
He said: "Entering the water, one sees a tall man.
He ascended the hall and said: "Leaves fall and return to the root; when coming, there was no mouth. The wondrous secret of the immortals is not transmitted even between father and son.
But how can one speak a phrase that takes up the hand? Add a little where there is too much; subtract a little where there is too little."
Ascending the hall: "Today is the fifteenth. As I ascend the hall, I raise it directly: the full host and the full guest.
The lanterns and the pillars are neither Buddhas nor patriarchs. Raising the two eyebrows, at the third watch the sun stands at noon."
Ascending the hall for the Buddha-bath ceremony: On this day every year, they splash foul water; this matter originated with Siddhārtha.
He himself claimed, "I alone am honored throughout the world," yet who among his descendants of later generations manages you?
Ascending the hall, he raised this topic: "The scriptures say, 'If one claims that the Tathāgata has preached any Dharma, one slanders the Buddha.
Yet, consider the Yellow-Faced Old Man’s seven locations and nine assemblies—what business was there to be done? The water rises and the boat goes higher."
Ascending the hall, he raised an example, saying: "Master Yunmen said, 'The Old Śākyamuni and Śakra, Lord of Devas, were arguing over the Buddha-dharma in the courtyard;

it was quite a commotion. The Master said: 'Master Yunmen is very much like a clever wife who, in her leisure, makes noodles when there is no flour. Nevertheless, everyone lacks one part without it.'"
Ascending the hall: Suddenly raining, suddenly sunny; the heavens are level, the earth is level. Śākyamuni and Maitreya have lost their eyesight.
(He lets out a shout. He descends from his seat.

Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, struck it once, and said: "The Buddhas of the three periods, the patriarchs of successive generations, the myriad phenomena of the ten thousand forms, humans, animals, grasses, and shrubs—all are here.
To let them loose is up to me; to gather them together is also up to me. He struck it again and said:
"Because I see you all, unconsciously and unknowingly, I have mounted the Buddha Hall backward and walked out through the triple gates."
[He] struck the sounding block once more.
He descended from his seat. [Then he] ascended the hall and said: "Master Muzhou ascended the seat and said, 'Head Seat?
The reply was, 'Present. Again he said, 'Abbot? The reply was, 'Present. 'Rector? The reply was, 'Present. These three parts are distinct; today we are at the first. Hereafter..."
The text is long; I shall leave it for another day. The Master said: "Lending one's hand to perform a fist-punch, startling the crowd and moving the multitude.
A guest of the Dragon Gate knows before the move is even made. Were it not so, Lingyin would suffer a loss."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following] for discussion: "The ancients said: 'Before the fifteenth day, you must not stay here with me;
if you stay here with me, I have a锥 (chui) to prick you. After the fifteenth day, you must not leave here with me;
if you leave here with me, I have a 鉤 (gou) to hook you. Right at the fifteenth day itself, when would one use the 锥 and when would one use the 鉤?"
This is it. The Master said: "A single character does not admit of a stroke.
He ascended the hall and said: "Seeing a corner through a wall, one knows it is an ox; seeing smoke from a mountain, one knows it is fire.
